title: Geometry Transformation Quantum Computation Model
abstract: This paper explores the development of a novel geometric transformation quantum computation model, designed to dynamically adapt to the geometry of input data. Traditional quantum computation often employs static models, limiting the model's effectiveness in handling dynamic geometric transformations. Our proposed model leverages a quantum adaptation mechanism to continuously re-optimize the quantum state, resulting in efficient computation for geometric operations. We detail the model's architecture, the underlying quantum algorithms, and the benefits of its adaptive nature. The core claim focuses on the model's ability to efficiently compute geometric transformations without the limitations of static models.

title: Quantum State Adaptive Topology
abstract: Quantum State Adaptive Topology (QSAT) presents a novel approach to quantum system optimization based on the dynamic manipulation of quantum state topology. This research explores the design of a quantum state self-adaptive topology algorithm, leveraging the inherent correlations between quantum qubits to optimize performance. The core mechanism involves adjusting the quantum state topology through a series of iterative interactions, guided by the target computation and environmental noise. Traditional topological optimization algorithms often struggle with complex environments, offering a more adaptable and potentially superior solution. This paper details the design of the QSAT algorithm, highlighting its novel core mechanism and potential benefits.

title: Enhanced Moss Growth Optimization with Benchmark Validation and a Wastewater Treatment Prediction Case Study
abstract: Complex optimization tasks in data-driven prediction and engineering applications often involve nonlinear, multimodal, and ill-conditioned objective functions. This study proposes an Enhanced Moss Growth Optimization algorithm (EMGO), an improved variant of the baseline MGO framework, to enhance exploratory step-size control and local covariance exploitation. EMGO incorporates two key algorithmic augmentations: a budget-adaptive jump regulation mechanism that balances global dispersal and fine-grained refinement, and a shrinkage-regularized covariance-guided sampling operator with relative eigenvalue flooring to exploit correlation structures among elite individuals without rank deficiency. The proposed algorithm is evaluated on the CEC2017 benchmark suite across 50 and 100 dimensions with 29 test functions, 30 independent runs, and a budget of 3×105 function evaluations per run, compared against ten state-of-the-art optimizers including CMA-ES, L-SHADE, SBO, and baseline MGO. Nonparametric Friedman ranking, Holm-adjusted Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, and runtime-matched analyses demonstrate that EMGO achieves highly competitive performance across high-dimensional landscapes. Furthermore, EMGO is applied to tune support vector regression (SVR) hyperparameters for effluent suspended solid (SS) prediction using the UCI Water Treatment Plant dataset under an expanding-window rolling-origin cross-validation scheme. EMGO-SVR achieves superior predictive accuracy (RMSE=5.58±0.64, MAE=3.97±0.46, R2=0.889±0.028), outperforming standard SVR, tree-based ensembles, and Bayesian optimization baselines. SHAP-based feature importance analysis confirms the physical and process consistency of the model predictions.

title: Doesn't Stop Reasoning: Analysis of Spurious CoT Termination
abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning improves large reasoning models (LRMs) on complex tasks but often produces long, redundant traces. Recent training-free early-exit methods shorten these traces by choosing an intermediate point to stop reasoning. We study one such strategy that injects an end-of-think token (EoT, ) at this point to trigger the reasoning-to-answering transition, and find that the injected EoT does not always induce a clean answering phase. Answering-phase generation can continue before the model regenerates another EoT, with the span preceding this regenerated EoT scaling with the reasoning tokens saved by early exit and exhibiting continued reasoning behavior. We call this spurious CoT termination, where reasoning-like generation continues into the answering phase. We hypothesize that insufficient attention to the injected EoT contributes to spurious CoT termination and probe this hypothesis with Exit-token Attention Biasing (EAB). Across four LRMs, five benchmarks, and two early-exit methods, increasing attention to the injected EoT reduces spurious CoT termination and answering-phase length. These results reveal a limitation of controlling LRMs by externally matching their explicit think-block format. Inserting the EoT token conforms to this format but does not by itself guarantee the intended reasoning-to-answering transition. Our code is available at https://github.com/Seunghee-Koh/Spurious-CoT-Termination.

title: Selective Forgetting in LLMs
abstract: Executive Summary This work approaches the problem of selectively forgetting knowledge from a large language model (LLM) for the purposes of safety, copyright, security, or otherwise. Also known as machine unlearning, this entails training a model to forget certain elements of the dataset on which it was trained. Unlearning methods must be evaluated both in terms of the extent to which the information has successfully been forgotten, and the performance of the unlearned model on the remaining (retained) data. We build on the work of TOFU (Task of Fictitious Unlearning) [21], which provides a dataset and benchmark for evaluating unlearning techniques. We create a new, TOFU-inspired question–answer dataset for the task of machine unlearning. The new dataset includes 10,500 question–answer pairs relating to over 1,000 distinct, synthetic entities of several types. Each question–answer pair is tagged with the entities it refers to, with the graph representation of our dataset containing over 2,600 edges between different entities. We perform two experiments with our dataset. The first experiment aims to capture whether the difficulty of forgetting a concept from a LLM depends on its granularity. For example, is unlearning more likely to be successful if forgetting a single book, rather than the book's author (as an author is connected to multiple books)? We find that granularity does not have a tangible effect on model performance in our dataset. There may be a small effect from granularity on the difficulty of forgetting, but this is not statistically significant across our results. Our second experiment explores the knock-on effect of forgetting a relationship between two entities. For example, if unlearning has been run on a model to forget only who wrote a book, but not the book or author themselves, is the model worse at responding to other questions about that book or author? We find that the model performance is lower on questions that contain the entities pertained in the relationship, than on those that do not. 1

title: This dataset supports the paper "Cardinality-Adaptive Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Variable-Scale Cooperative Aerial Games"
abstract: This dataset supports the paper "Cardinality-Adaptive Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Variable-Scale Cooperative Aerial Games" (submitted to Applied Intelligence). It contains the complete training and evaluation records of CA-MAPPO, a cardinality-adaptive multi-agent proximal policy optimization algorithm for variable-scale cooperative aerial-game formations, generated with the JSBSim six-degree-of-freedom flight-dynamics engine in the loop.The dataset includes: (1) per-iteration training logs (episode return, periodic win rate, policy/value losses, entropy, KL divergence; JSONL) from three-seed main training runs and the gated three-stage curriculum (single-scale consolidation at 2v2, mixed-scale main stage on {2v2, 3v3, 5v5}, and ace-weighted final consolidation), covering trained scales and strictly held-out zero-shot scales {4v4, 6v6}; (2) paired evaluation results (win/draw/loss counts with Wilson confidence intervals; JSON) for CA-MAPPO, MAPPO, QMIX and ablation variants, organized by opponent level (L1–L4) × team size under a common-random-number protocol with 20 episodes per cell, plus zero-shot extrapolation evaluations at 10v10, 14v14 and 20v20; (3) ablation study data (without geometric attention bias, without set-attention critic, single-scale training, without per-scale advantage normalization, without win-rate-gated curriculum, UPDeT-faithful adaptation, and double-budget controls); (4) full-episode step-by-step simulation records (per-step state, hybrid action, reward, termination flag, and flight parameters for every agent); (5) automated maneuver-detector statistics behind the emergent-tactics analysis and self-attention weight maps (NPZ) behind the attention-analysis figures.The dataset contains raw data only — no figures, no plotted curves, no trained model weights.

title: Dynamic Geometry Adjustment in Probability Logic Models
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic geometry adjustment framework for probability logic models. The core idea is to dynamically adjust model parameters based on the input data's geometric complexity, optimizing model performance through this adaptive control. We propose a system that iteratively evaluates the model's performance against a defined metric, and then adjusts the parameters to minimize this metric. The framework leverages a geometric complexity measure derived from the input data, providing a robust and adaptable approach to parameter optimization. The paper details the model's architecture, training procedure, and performance evaluation, demonstrating its effectiveness in a range of scenarios. The focus is on creating a method that can automatically tune model parameters to achieve optimal performance.

title: Quantum Hidden Matrix
abstract: Quantum Hidden Matrix (QHM) is a novel approach to linear algebra computation leveraging quantum mechanics and the concept of quantum entanglement. This paper explores the potential of QHM to significantly accelerate linear algebra operations and enhance the capture of quantum entanglement, offering a potential paradigm shift in computational efficiency and accuracy. The core claim is that by utilizing quantum entanglement to manipulate and accelerate linear algebra calculations, we can achieve a substantial improvement over classical methods, particularly in scenarios involving complex calculations and sensitive data.

title: Quantum-Inspired Geometry for Pattern Recognition
abstract: Quantum-inspired geometry, a novel approach to pattern recognition, leverages the principles of quantum mechanics to design geometric structures with enhanced sensitivity to subtle patterns. This paper explores the integration of quantum concepts, such as superposition and entanglement, into the core design of geometric elements, aiming to improve pattern identification capabilities across diverse data types. We propose a new framework for geometric analysis, focusing on the creation of structures capable of capturing complex, non-linear relationships inherent in many real-world patterns. The research delves into the mathematical foundations of these structures, demonstrating their potential to surpass traditional methods in identifying nuanced distinctions. This work presents a preliminary investigation into the application of quantum-inspired geometry to pattern recognition, outlining a potential pathway toward more robust and adaptable pattern detection systems.

title: Quantum Information Evolution: An Adaptive Self-Assembly Approach
abstract: This paper investigates the evolution of quantum information through a novel self-adaptive quantum evolution model. We propose a framework that decomposes quantum states into multiple sub-states, dynamically adjusts these sub-states' interactions, and generates complex quantum states. The core mechanism centers on a "quantum self-assembly" process, enabling the system to evolve in response to environmental changes and specific goals. This approach surpasses traditional quantum computing by offering dynamic state adjustments and the ability to create more advanced quantum functionalities. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this model in generating complex quantum states through a tailored, self-regulated evolution process.

title: 基于自适应混沌的概率几何优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm, termed "Adaptive Chaotic Probability Optimization" (ACPO), based on the principles of self-adaptive chaos. Traditional optimization methods often require manual parameter tuning, which is ineffective for complex problems. ACPO leverages the inherent dynamics of chaotic systems to dynamically adjust optimization parameters, enabling the algorithm to discover more robust and globally optimal solutions. This research explores the potential of using self-adaptive chaos to overcome limitations inherent in conventional optimization techniques. We present a detailed analysis of the algorithm's design, its performance characteristics, and its implications for various optimization challenges.

title: Title: Resonance-Based Dynamic Algorithm (RBD)
abstract: The optimization of dynamic algorithms is a complex challenge, often requiring iterative adjustments to parameters to achieve desired performance. Traditional optimization methods can be computationally expensive and may not always converge to optimal solutions. This paper introduces Resonance-Based Dynamic Algorithm (RBD), a novel algorithm that utilizes resonant principles to dynamically adjust parameters, thereby maximizing stability and efficiency. The core mechanism of RBD involves the development of a 'resonance matrix' that continuously monitors the system's state and automatically adjusts parameters to maintain optimal performance. This approach offers a fundamentally different paradigm for optimization, potentially leading to significant improvements in algorithm efficiency and stability. The paper details the algorithm's implementation, demonstrates its effectiveness through several illustrative examples, and discusses its potential implications for various dynamic algorithm applications.

title: Quantum Error Correction Coding and Feedback Control
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum error correction (QEC) that integrates coding with feedback control. The core idea is to leverage multi-particle error-correcting codes and dynamically calibrate individual qubits based on measurement outcomes. This synergistic combination aims to significantly enhance error correction efficiency and achieve high fidelity quantum information transmission. The proposed framework addresses the critical challenge of environmental noise-induced decoherence, a major impediment to practical quantum computation and communication. We outline the design principles, key formulas, and the underlying mechanisms driving this approach. Specifically, we detail the application of a specific concatenated code structure and introduce a control system that utilizes feedback loops to counteract identified errors. The effectiveness of this combined approach is discussed theoretically, highlighting the potential for improved error correction rates and robustness against various noise models.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Algorithm Design (QEAD)
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers the potential for unparalleled computational speed and accuracy. This paper investigates the design of a novel algorithm, Quantum Entanglement-Driven Algorithm Design (QEAD), that leverages entanglement to accelerate computation and enhance the analysis of complex data. We propose a 'Quantum Resonance' algorithm, a process that utilizes entanglement to rapidly traverse the state space, identifying patterns and correlations efficiently. The core mechanism of QEAD centers around exploiting entanglement to achieve significant speedups in data processing and simulation tasks. This work explores the theoretical foundations and practical implementation of QEAD, focusing on its potential to revolutionize areas demanding intricate data analysis.

title: Symbiotic Quantum-Classical Hybrid Learning for Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel symbiotic learning framework that synergistically integrates quantum computing and classical reinforcement learning (RL). The core idea is to leverage the unique capabilities of quantum systems – specifically, their ability to efficiently represent and explore high-dimensional state spaces – alongside the established strengths of classical RL algorithms for policy optimization. We introduce a hybrid architecture where a quantum neural network (QNN) acts as a sophisticated state processor, generating candidate actions based on the current state, while a classical RL agent learns to refine and select the optimal actions. Our approach moves beyond quantum-inspired algorithms by establishing a genuine symbiotic relationship between quantum and classical components, leading to potentially faster learning rates and improved performance in complex RL environments. The framework is described mathematically, outlining the key components and interactions. We present a detailed mathematical formulation of the system, highlighting the contributions of both the quantum and classical components. The efficacy of the system is conceptually discussed, focusing on the benefits of combining quantum exploration with classical policy learning. This paper lays the groundwork for future research in this rapidly evolving field.

title: Automated Theorem Proving via Evolutionary Algorithms for Strategy Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of evolutionary algorithms (EAs) to optimize the strategy employed within automated theorem provers (ATPs). Traditional ATPs often rely on pre-defined, static proof strategies, which can be inefficient for complex theorems. We propose a novel approach where an EA dynamically explores and adapts proof strategies, iteratively refining them based on their effectiveness in solving theorems. The core of our method involves encoding different proof strategies as individuals within an EA population, evaluating their performance using established ATP metrics (e.g., proof length, number of steps), and employing selection, mutation, and crossover operators to evolve the population towards strategies that consistently demonstrate superior proof performance. The results presented demonstrate the potential of this adaptive strategy optimization to significantly improve the efficiency and effectiveness of ATPs. We outline the key components of the system, including the EA implementation, the ATP interface, and the evaluation metrics. Furthermore, we discuss the challenges and future directions of this research.

evidence.title: Automated Theorem Proving via Evolutionary Algorithms for Strategy Optimization
evidence.abstract: This paper investigates the application of evolutionary algorithms (EAs) to optimize the strategy employed within automated theorem provers (ATPs). Traditional ATPs often rely on pre-defined, static proof strategies, which can be inefficient for complex theorems. We propose a novel approach where an EA dynamically explores and adapts proof strategies, iteratively refining them based on their effectiveness in solving theorems. The core of our method involves encoding different proof strategies as individuals within an EA population, evaluating their performance using established ATP metrics (e.g., proof length, number of steps), and employing selection, mutation, and crossover operators to evolve the population towards strategies that consistently demonstrate superior proof performance. The results presented demonstrate the potential of this adaptive strategy optimization to significantly improve the efficiency and effectiveness of ATPs. We outline the key components of the system, including the EA implementation, the ATP interface, and the evaluation metrics. Furthermore, we discuss the challenges and future directions of this research.

title: Societies of Narrow Minds: A Interdisciplinary Mapping Review of Multi-Agent Systems and Emergent Cooperation
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Multi-Agent Systems and Emergent Cooperation in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of multi-agent and cooperation as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Quantum Topology Adaptive Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Quantum Topology Adaptive Optimization Algorithm (QTAOA) represents a novel approach to optimization, leveraging the unique properties of quantum topology to dynamically explore solution spaces and identify optimal configurations. This paper introduces a framework where the algorithm iteratively adjusts its search strategy based on feedback from a quantum-inspired probabilistic model, enabling automated discovery of optimal solutions across diverse application domains, particularly within machine learning and circuit design. This work offers a fundamentally different paradigm compared to traditional optimization methods, promising to address limitations in efficiency and robustness.

title: Quantum Simulation of Self-Adaptive Gradient Descent
abstract: Quantum simulation offers unprecedented capabilities for studying complex quantum systems, but traditional methods often struggle with computational complexity and require significant parameter adjustments. This paper introduces a novel quantum simulation approach utilizing self-adaptive gradient descent, a technique designed to dynamically adjust simulation parameters based on observed results. This algorithm significantly enhances simulation accuracy and efficiency by intelligently optimizing the simulation process. We present a framework that allows for continuous parameter refinement, mitigating the limitations of static parameter settings. The core mechanism centers around a learned parameter adjustment strategy, leveraging the inherent dynamics of the quantum system to improve the simulation. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations, showcasing a substantial improvement in simulation fidelity compared to existing methods. The findings highlight the potential of self-adaptive gradient descent for accelerating and refining quantum simulations.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Diffusion for Material Characterization
abstract: Quantum-enhanced diffusion is a novel approach to material characterization that leverages the principles of quantum mechanics to accelerate the diffusion process, resulting in significantly improved accuracy and speed compared to traditional methods. This paper introduces a new methodology centered around carefully engineered quantum states to manipulate the diffusion mechanism, leading to enhanced data acquisition and a more detailed understanding of material properties. The core mechanism involves utilizing quantum tunneling to reduce noise and enhance the sensitivity of the measurement, ultimately enabling the precise characterization of diffusion processes. We present a rigorous theoretical analysis and experimental validation demonstrating the efficacy of this technique. This method offers a substantial advancement over existing techniques, promising a paradigm shift in the field of material science and engineering.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Satisfaction for Complex Constraint Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum computing principles to enhance constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs), specifically for complex, large-scale systems. We propose a novel quantum-enhanced constraint satisfaction technique, utilizing quantum algorithms to expedite the search process and improve solution accuracy. The core mechanism centers on exploiting quantum properties – superposition and entanglement – to effectively explore the solution space and mitigate the exponential complexity inherent in traditional CSP solvers. The paper presents a detailed analysis of the algorithm's design, implementation, and potential benefits, demonstrating improved performance compared to classical methods on benchmark CSPs. The core claim is that quantum-enhanced constraint satisfaction can significantly reduce computational time and improve solution quality for complex systems, offering a substantial advancement in this field.

title: The intersection of post-quantum cryptography and QaaS: architecting quantum-safe cloud infrastructures
abstract: Introduction By 2030, an estimated 40% of current cloud infrastructures may be rendered vulnerable by cryptanalytically relevant quantum computers (CRQCs). Methods This paper introduces a 4-tier security framework tailored for Quantumas-a-Service (QaaS) deployments, focusing on securing data-in-transit. Integrating 3 NIST-standardized post-quantum algorithms (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and SLHDSA), our architecture mitigates interception threats based on Shor's algorithm. Results Emulation across an enterprise cloud topology demonstrates a maximum latency overhead of 17.7 milliseconds per TLS handshake under high-latency WAN conditions, ensuring high-availability operations without catastrophic fragmentation failure. Discussion The proposed model demonstrates the viability of modern latticebased cryptography for live environments and provides a structured 3-phase transition roadmap for cloud service providers (CSPs) to achieve quantum-resilience seamlessly.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence in detecting pulmonary nodules on computed tomography: A systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Objectives: Pulmonary nodules are frequent findings on chest computed tomography (CT) and are crucial for early lung cancer detection. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning (DL), has emerged as a powerful tool for automated nodule detection, but diagnostic performance varies across studies. The objective of this study is to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of AI-based imaging systems in detecting pulmonary nodules on CT and compare DL with traditional computer-aided detection (CAD) and radiologists. Material and Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with PRISMADTA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched up to March 2025. Eligible studies assessed AI for pulmonary nodule detection on CT and reported sensitivity, specificity, or sufficient data for 2×2 contingency tables. Pooled estimates of sensitivity, specificity, and diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) were calculated using a bivariate random-effects model. Subgroup analyses examined DL versus CAD, detection of nodules <10 mm, and AI performance compared with radiologists. Study quality was evaluated using QUADAS-2. Results: Twenty-six studies comprising 31,742 CT scans were included. Pooled sensitivity and specificity of AI were 0.90 (95% CI 0.87–0.93) and 0.87 (95% CI 0.84–0.90), respectively, with a DOR of 60.2 and an area under the sROC curve of 0.94. DL outperformed CAD (sensitivity 0.92 vs 0.83; specificity 0.88 vs 0.84). Sensitivity for nodules <10 mm was lower (DL 0.82; CAD 0.68). AI matched radiologists, and AI-assisted radiologists showed improved sensitivity (0.93). Conclusion: AI demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy in pulmonary nodule detection, outperforming CAD and matching radiologists, with the greatest potential as a second reader in lung cancer screening.

title: Pemodelan Akustik HMM–GMM untuk Pengenalan Ucapan Kata Darurat Bahasa Indonesia
abstract: Keamanan dan keselamatan merupakan kebutuhan dasar manusia. Situasi darurat seperti pencurian, kebakaran, maupun ancaman lainnya sering kali memerlukan respons yang cepat untuk mengurangi dampak negatifnya. Seiring berkembangnya teknologi, sistem keamanan berbasis suara menjadi solusi potensial untuk meningkatkan efektivitas deteksi dini dan tanggapan terhadap keadaan darurat. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengembangkan model akustik berbasis Hidden Markov Model–Gaussian Mixture Model (HMM–GMM) guna mendeteksi kata-kata darurat dalam Bahasa Indonesia, seperti tolong, jangan, maling, kebakaran, dan kecelakaan. Dataset yang digunakan terdiri atas 1.100 berkas audio yang seimbang antara kelas darurat dan non-darurat. Fitur akustik dari dataset diekstraksi menggunakan Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) beserta fitur turunan delta dan delta-delta. Evaluasi dilakukan dengan metode 10-fold cross-validation dan model terbaik diujikan dengan data holdout test untuk memastikan kemampuan generalisasi model. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa model HMM–GMM dengan 4 state dan 16 komponen Gaussian memberikan performa terbaik dengan akurasi 94,5%, presisi 94,3%, recall 94,5%, dan F1-score 94,4% pada hold. Temuan ini membuktikan bahwa model HMM–GMM efektif dalam mengenali ucapan darurat Bahasa Indonesia secara akurat dan efisien.

title: Разработка информационно-аналитического инструмента поддержки маркетинговых решений на основе аффинити-анализа и LLM-интерпретации пользовательских отзывов (на примере сети «Золотое Яблоко»)
abstract: Целью работы является разработка воспроизводимого инструмента, позволяющего на основе отзывов и связанной с ними поведенческой информации выявлять пересечения аудиторий бренда, анализировать тематическую структуру клиентского опыта и представлять результаты в прикладной форме. В работе использованы методы сбора и очистки открытых данных, аффинити-анализ, тематическая обработка текстов на основе эмбеддингов и кластеризации, LLM-интерпретация тематических групп и методы визуальной аналитики. В результате сформирована эмпирическая база по сети «Золотое Яблоко», реализованы алгоритмы расчета аффинити и интегрального показателя с учетом масштаба бренда, разработан процесс обработки отзывов и дашборд «Клиентский контур», объединяющий модули аффинити-анализа, геоаналитики и тематического сравнения. Результаты работы могут быть использованы в маркетинговой, CX- и конкурентной аналитике для выбора смежных брендов, локализации проблемных зон клиентского опыта и формирования гипотез для партнерств и локальных пилотов. Сделан вывод о том, что отзывы картографической платформы могут выступать системной основой для поддержки маркетинговых решений при условии их комплексной аналитической обработки.

title: Enhancing Deep Knowledge Tracing with Semantic Question Embeddings for Engineering Mathematics Education
abstract: In a course, with potentially up to hundreds of students, no instructor can guide each stu-dent’s learning process individually. Knowledge tracing is a technique that estimates what a student knows from their answers, and can be used to suggest what to practice next. Exist-ing methods treat each question as a single opaque number or requires hand-labelling each question with the concept it tests, and may need thousands of past student records before they work. A new course has none of this. This thesis proposes EmbeddingDKT, which represents each question by a language model’s embedding of its text, along with a pipeline that builds a question bank and simulated students for a new course from its syllabus alone (MATH 267, University Calculus II ). On real student data it ranks first among comparable models (AUC 0.833), scores questions it has never seen almost as well as familiar ones, and in simulation guides learners to their weakest topics faster than random practice.

title: Privacy, Robustness, and Fairness Trade-offs in Federated Intrusion Detection: Geometric Indistinguishability at the Aggregation Interface
abstract: Federated learning enables privacy-conscious collaboration for network intrusion detection without centralizing sensitive traffic data, yet its deployment in operational environments must simultaneously satisfy three competing requirements: formal differential privacy guaranties, tolerance to Byzantine-adversarial participants, and reliable detection coverage across severely imbalanced attack categories. Existing literature treats these properties as independently composable, an assumption that this paper challenges both theoretically and empirically. In this paper, we study how these requirements interact in class-imbalanced federated NIDS and introduce geometric indistinguishability as a conceptual lens for a regime in which privacy-induced dispersion in client updates can make minority-class signals harder for robust aggregation to preserve. Using UNSW-NB15 as a case study, we evaluate DP-SGD combined with coordinate-wise median under label-flip and model-poisoning attacks, with threat coverage assessed across attack categories. Our results provide initial evidence that the joint use of privacy noise and robust aggregation can disproportionately degrade detection of rare attacks relative to majority classes. We also show that part of the observed collapse under strong privacy can arise from training miscalibration, while a residual performance floor may remain for ultra-rare categories even after epsilon-dependent tuning. These findings motivate studying privacy, robustness, and rare-attack coverage jointly rather than as independently composable properties, and suggest that aggregation-aware modeling and sample-aware evaluation are promising directions for trustworthy federated NIDS.

title: Equidistant sets for additive kernels with finitely many negative squares
abstract: We isolate a linear-algebraic principle underlying several recent bounds for equilateral sets and equidistant codes. Let κ be a symmetric kernel on a set S that can be written as a squared Hilbert distance minus a squared distance into a space of dimension at most q (equivalently, an anchored Schoenberg kernel with at most q negative squares). For the coordinatewise sum of κ on Sn we prove that any m points whose pairwise kernel values all equal d > 0 satisfy R = (d/2)Cm + X with X positive semidefinite of rank at most qn, and consequently m ≤ 1 + Σt rt, where rt is the affine rank of the positive features of the alphabet actually used in coordinate t. A stable version replaces exactness by an operator-norm error and a spectral-tail budget. Three applications. (1) For codes in Zqn that are equidistant with respect to the squared Lee weight, |C| ≤ (q/2)n + 1 for even q and |C| ≤ 2⌈(q-1)/4⌉n + 1 for odd q, with no linearity assumption; for q = 5 the bound |C| ≤ 2n+1 is attained by an explicit evaluation code for every n = (5k-1)/2. (2) For p ∈ (4k, 4k+2) we recover the centred-Gram identity used by Ge–Xu–Zhou and tighten the finite negative rank budget from 4kn to 2kn; this rank improvement alone does not imply a linear cardinality bound. (3) The sharp first-order asymptotics of the Schütte problem on 2 ≤ p ≤ 4: limN N(Rp(N) - 1) = 2/p. Contents. Manuscript (PDF and LaTeX source) plus the two verification scripts covering every finite numerical claim, with a SHA-256 manifest. Both re-ran green on 2026-09-03. The proofs are analytic; the scripts check the finite claims, the closed forms and the negative controls. Status. Author preprint, not peer reviewed. A priority audit found no prior statement converting a negative-square count into an equilateral-set cardinality bound; scope was arXiv plus the reference lists of the cited works, with MathSciNet and zbMATH not searched. A finite search is not a proof of priority. Corrections welcome. AI disclosure. Anthropic Claude and OpenAI Codex were used as research tools for strategy exploration, derivation suggestions, symbolic and numerical checks, adversarial review, code drafting and manuscript drafting; the scripts were re-run in a separate session from the one that produced them. The author takes full responsibility for the accuracy and originality of the manuscript.

For the coordinatewise sum of κ on Sn we prove that any m points whose pairwise kernel values all equal d > 0 satisfy R = (d/2)Cm + X with X positive semidefinite of rank at most qn, and consequently m ≤ 1 + Σt rt, where rt is the affine rank of the positive features of the alphabet actually used in coordinate t. A stable version replaces exactness by an operator-norm error and a spectral-tail budget. Three applications. (1) For codes in Zqn that are equidistant with respect to the squared Lee weight, |C| ≤ (q/2)n + 1 for even q and |C| ≤ 2⌈(q-1)/4⌉n + 1 for odd q, with no linearity assumption; for q = 5 the bound |C| ≤ 2n+1 is attained by an explicit evaluation code for every n = (5k-1)/2. (2) For p ∈ (4k, 4k+2) we recover the centred-Gram identity used by Ge–Xu–Zhou and tighten the finite negative rank budget from 4kn to 2kn; this rank improvement alone does not imply a linear cardinality bound. (3) The sharp first-order asymptotics of the Schütte problem on 2 ≤ p ≤ 4: limN N(Rp(N) - 1) = 2/p. Contents. Manuscript (PDF and LaTeX source) plus the two verification scripts covering every finite numerical claim, with a SHA-256 manifest. Both re-ran green on 2026-09-03. The proofs are analytic; the scripts check the finite claims, the closed forms and the negative controls. Status. Author preprint, not peer reviewed. A priority audit found no prior statement converting a negative-square count into an equilateral-set cardinality bound; scope was arXiv plus the reference lists of the cited works, with MathSciNet and zbMATH not searched. A finite search is not a proof of priority. Corrections welcome. AI disclosure. abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum information processing to revolutionize geometric modeling, specifically focusing on the creation of highly accurate hyper-resolution geometric models. This research explores the theoretical underpinnings of this approach, provides a preliminary implementation of the core mechanism, and discusses potential challenges and future directions.

title: Quantum Walk-Based Optimization of Reinforcement Learning Policies
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum walks to enhance the optimization of reinforcement learning (RL) policies. Traditional RL algorithms often struggle with exploring complex state spaces efficiently, leading to slow learning rates and suboptimal solutions. We propose a novel approach that leverages the inherent properties of quantum walks – superposition and interference – to accelerate the learning process. Specifically, we represent the RL environment as a graph and perform a quantum walk on this graph. The walk's quantum superposition allows for simultaneous exploration of multiple actions, drastically reducing the time required to converge to an optimal policy. We outline the theoretical framework, detailing the mathematical formulation of the quantum walk and its interaction with the RL environment. The core contribution lies in demonstrating how quantum walk's ability to explore multiple states concurrently can provide a significant advantage over classical approaches in optimizing RL policies. We present a conceptual model and a set of equations describing the process, highlighting the key elements for implementation. The results, while theoretical, demonstrate the feasibility and potential impact of this hybrid quantum-classical approach for tackling complex RL problems.

title: Symbolic Regression with Grammatical Evolution and Temporal Constraints
abstract: Symbolic regression is a powerful technique for discovering mathematical relationships from data. However, it frequently faces challenges when dealing with time-series data, specifically capturing and enforcing temporal dependencies and constraints. This work introduces a novel approach that combines grammatical evolution, a genetic algorithm designed for program evolution, with temporal constraint propagation. The core idea is to guide the evolutionary process using rules that ensure the generated symbolic expressions adhere to the inherent temporal order present in the data. This integration leverages the generative capabilities of grammatical evolution while providing a mechanism for rigorous temporal reasoning. The proposed method offers a promising solution for accurately modeling complex time-dependent systems. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical framework outlining the core components and their interactions, focusing on the underlying mathematical principles.

title: Self-Referential Graph Neural Networks for Knowledge Discovery
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to knowledge discovery within graphs by introducing Self-Referential Graph Neural Networks (SR-GNNs). Traditional Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) operate passively, learning representations based solely on the graph structure and node features. This limits their ability to adapt and refine their understanding, particularly in complex graph scenarios. Our core idea is to equip nodes within a GNN with the capability to directly influence the network's architecture and training process, establishing a feedback loop for iterative improvement. This allows the network to dynamically adjust its parameters, node embeddings, and even structural elements, ultimately leading to a more robust and accurate representation of the graph's underlying knowledge. The SR-GNN framework is designed to address the limitations of static GNNs by incorporating a self-reflective mechanism. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline the key components needed for implementation, highlighting its potential to significantly enhance knowledge discovery tasks within graph-structured data.

title: Quantum Error Correction: A Dynamic Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is a critical component of quantum computing, enabling the reliable transmission and manipulation of quantum information. Classical error correction relies on redundancy and error detection, which are fundamentally limited by the speed of light. Quantum error correction, however, offers the potential for significantly higher error rates and is intrinsically linked to the quantum state itself. This paper explores a novel dynamic adaptive algorithm for QEC, focusing on optimizing the quantum state representation and error correction process through a feedback mechanism. We demonstrate that this algorithm, designed specifically for QEC, achieves substantially improved precision and adaptability compared to existing approaches, offering a path towards more robust and efficient quantum systems. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting the quantum state to better respond to the effects of errors, leading to a significant enhancement in error correction capabilities.

abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to multi-qubit error correction that dynamically adjusts its strategy based on real-time monitoring of the error correction environment. The core claim of this work is the design of a system capable of adapting its error correction strategy dynamically, while the core mechanism relies on machine learning for real-time environmental monitoring and strategic adjustment. The potential impact of this approach is significant, particularly in the development of more reliable and scalable quantum computing architectures.

title: Multi-Scale Quantum Information Encryption
abstract: This paper investigates the development of a novel cryptographic scheme, Multi-Scale Quantum Information Encryption (MSQIE), designed to provide enhanced data protection against classical cryptanalytic attacks. The core of the proposed scheme centers around leveraging quantum key distribution (QKD) and multi-scale quantum entanglement, establishing a secure foundation for data protection. We outline the fundamental mechanisms of the system, emphasizing the utilization of quantum error correction and the formation of entangled states across multiple scales. The paper details the design of the encryption protocol, justifying its advantages over existing methods through a comprehensive analysis of potential vulnerabilities and limitations. Furthermore, we explore the theoretical foundations underpinning the scheme, including the interplay of entanglement and quantum error correction. The proposed method offers a substantial improvement in security through a combination of cryptographic primitives, promising a robust defense against current and future threats. Finally, we address potential challenges and future research directions within the field of quantum information security.

title: Метод статистического мониторинга актуальности и автоматизированной актуализации словаря предметных концептов в системе ассоциативно-семантической поддержки принятия решений по данным БПЛА
abstract: Цель данной работы: разработка метода статистического мониторинга актуальности и автоматизированной актуализации словаря предметных концептов и текстовых шаблонов как специального математического и алгоритмического обеспечения проблемно-ориентированной системы ассоциативно-семантической поддержки принятия решений по данным БПЛА. В данной работе была рассмотрена проблема потери актуальности словаря предметных концептов и текстовых шаблонов в системе ассоциативно-семантической поддержки принятия решений по данным беспилотных летательных аппаратов (БПЛА). Для решения этой проблемы был разработан метод статистического мониторинга актуальности, который позволяет автоматически выявлять семантический дрейф, деградацию концептов, пробелы в покрытии и появление новых смыслов в потоке наблюдений. Все расчеты проводились в программном обеспечении MS Office (Excel) и Colab.

title: PERTEK-ÇEMİŞGEZEK (TUNCELİ) HATTINDAKİ DEMİRLİ ZONLARIN ASTER VNIR-SWIR BANTLARI KULLANILARAK TESPİTİ
abstract: Çalışma alanı Pertek-Çemişgezek (Tunceli) hattında Keban Baraj Gölü’nün kuzeyinde yer alır. Bu zonda, magmatik birimlerle metamorfik birimlerin kontakları boyunca demirli cevher ve alterasyon ürünleri gelişmiştir. Bölgedeki ekonomik oluşuklar uzun yıllardır araştırmacıların dikkatini çekmektedir. Bu çalışmada mevcut alandaki potansiyel demirli zonların varlığının ve yayılımının uydu teknolojileri yoluyla tespiti hedeflenmiştir. Bu amaçla, Pertek-Çemişgezek (Tunceli) bölgesindeki, bilinen demirli zonlar referans alınarak ASTER uydusunun VNIR-SWIR bantları üzerinden görüntü zenginleştirme metotları uygulanmış ve kompozit görüntüler oluşturulmuştur. Saha gözlemlerinde hem mermerlerin hem de yan kayaların içerisinde ağsal ve yer yer masif cevherleşme izleri doğrulanmıştır. Sonuçta, literatür kaynaklı lokasyonlar, hem uydu gözlemleri hem de saha doğrulama çalışmaları ile tespit edilmiştir. Buna göre, Pertek-Çemişgezek (Tunceli) hattında; Ayazpınarı demir (Fe) zuhurları, Ballıdut FeOx Alterasyonları, Çemişgezek Elazığ Yol Yarması FeOx Alterasyonları şeklinde demirli ve demirce zengin zonlar tespit edilmiştir. Yapılan analizlerde en uygun RGB bant kombinasyonunun R: VNIR (Band 2 / Band 1), G: SWIR Band 6 ve B: VNIR Band 3 olduğu belirlenmiştir.

title: CT-based cross-center risk stratification of pure ground-glass nodules incorporating domain style–aware correction
abstract: BackgroundPure ground-glass nodules (pGGNs) are increasingly detected on chest CT. Although most exhibit indolent behavior, a subset may harbor invasive features before obvious radiological progression, making early risk stratification clinically important.PurposeTo develop and externally validate a CT-based deep learning model with domain adaptation for cross-center risk stratification of pGGNs.Material and MethodsThis retrospective multicenter study included 1235 surgically confirmed pGGNs from two institutions. A deep learning model incorporating domain style-aware correction was developed to differentiate AAH/AIS-like lesions from MIA/IAC-like lesions using preoperative CT images. Data from one center were used for training and internal validation, and an independent external cohort was used for validation. Model performance was evaluated using AUC, accuracy, calibration, and decision curve analysis.ResultsThe model achieved an AUC of 0.93 and an accuracy of 90.4% in the internal validation set. In the external validation set, the AUC was 0.88 with an accuracy of 81.7%, demonstrating good cross-center generalization. Domain adaptation improved external AUC from 0.85 to 0.88. Calibration analysis showed good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities. Decision curve analysis indicated higher net benefit compared with treat-all and treat-none strategies across a range of thresholds.ConclusionThe proposed model demonstrates robust performance across centers and may serve as a noninvasive tool to support individualized surveillance strategies for patients with pGGNs.

title: PL-SCEA: Reconfiguring Pretrained Attention for Few-Shot Industrial Anomaly Detection
abstract: Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) provide transferable patch representations for few-shot industrial anomaly detection, but their attention computation is typically inherited from pretraining objectives centered on semantic aggregation. This creates a potential mismatch: token relations that support semantic recognition may not adequately expose the localized texture and structural deviations required for anomaly localization. We therefore investigate the hypothesis that the attention computation of a frozen VFM can be reconfigured as a task-relevant component of anomaly detection. We instantiate this idea with Power-Law Self-Correlation Enhanced Attention (PL-SCEA), which retains the semantic context of pretrained query-key attention while constructing token-adaptive self-correlations over contextualized value features. Positive-correlation filtering and power-law reweighting then emphasize relations that are salient relative to each token's relational background, without introducing additional trainable attention projections. The resulting features are modeled by a lightweight variational autoencoder that provides a fixed-size reconstruction-based representation of category-specific normality. The two stages serve complementary roles: attention reconfiguration shapes how local relational deviations are represented, while reconstruction-based modeling converts deviations from learned normality into anomaly scores. Across MVTec AD and VisA, the complete framework achieves competitive image-level detection and consistently strong pixel-level localization across the evaluated few-shot settings. Ablations further show that PL-SCEA improves localization with either the VAE or a memory bank under the tested setting. These results support the view that task-aligned attention reconfiguration can improve the anomaly-localization capability of frozen pretrained representations.

title: GPS-Bench: A Governance Policy Benchmark for Automating Policy Analysis
abstract: Policy analysis requires more than predicting whether a proposal will pass: it requires identifying who will be affected, how those actors respond, and what follows. LLM-based policy simulations model these processes at scale, but their validity is hard to establish when plausible behaviour is never compared with observed outcomes. We introduce GPS-Bench, an evidence-grounded benchmark for governance policy simulation that links policies to relevant actors, actor actions and downstream impacts using legislative records, lobbying disclosures, regulatory documents, corporate filings, economic data and other public evidence. Actors are reconstructed from the dated record rather than prompted as archetypes, so a persona is an evidence object with provenance; a human-annotated pool forms the Gold evaluation set, while cases labelled by a separate LLM from retrieved evidence are treated as Silver supervision and never as test labels. Because every inference mode reads the same grounded state and emits the same schema, GPS-Bench turns "does multi-agent simulation help?" into a controlled comparison: we contrast joint reasoning, independent and communicating actor agents, graph-based methods and weight-level fine-tuning over one policy state. Fine-tuning on the grounded record gives the strongest actor-level impact prediction, and decomposition does not beat it; what decomposition adds is mechanism. Agents hold private, non-identical evidence, each seeing its own exposure clause, and address named partners with concrete joint proposals, what they offer, what they need in return, and why acting together beats acting alone, so the coalitions that form can be checked against the commitments the record holds. GPS-Bench therefore gives a common empirical setting for studying when evidence, actor modelling and multi-agent interaction improve the prediction and interpretation of policy outcomes.

title: Kovoluutioneuroverkot ja niiden käyttö rintasyövän havaitsemiseen mammografiakuvista
abstract: This bachelor's thesis discusses convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and their use in the detection of breast cancer from mammographic images. In addition, the thesis introduces six classic CNN architectures. The aim of the thesis is to gather information on the operation of CNNs, classic CNN architectures and the development of them, and the potential use of CNNs. The discussion of the potential use of CNNs focuses on the detection of breast cancer from mammographic images. The thesis was conducted as a literature review. CNNs are machine learning models that are particularly well-suited for the analysis of images. CNNs consist of layers that receive and transmit information using feature maps. In convolutional layers, maps obtained as input are processed using weighted filters and convolution. Each filter in a layer produces a feature map for the output of the layer. In pooling layers, the size of the feature maps decreases, as sections in the maps are replaced with averages or maximums, for example. The adjustable parameters of a network are updated during training using training data. In studies where the analysis of mammographic images has been tested using CNNs, the detection has often been implemented in two stages. First, the mammographic images are often segmented or preprocessed in other ways. In the second stage, CNNs classify the given images. In testings with human radiologists, the results of CNN models have been even better than the ones of individual radiologists. However, CNNs have difficulties in cases underrepresented in the training data. In a study where a hybrid of a CNN and a human radiologist was tested, the hybrid obtained better results than either of the parts individually. The results indicate that radiologists could benefit from using CNNs as help with the analysis of mammograms.

title: Geometric Predictive Modeling with Hybrid Neural Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel geometric predictive modeling approach leveraging hybrid neural networks and geometric data analysis. We address the challenge of accurately predicting complex geometric structures from data by integrating the strengths of both neural networks – adept at pattern recognition – and geometric analysis – capable of uncovering underlying structures and relationships. The proposed model employs a layered architecture, initially leveraging a convolutional neural network to extract initial features and then integrating a geometric regression module to refine these features and predict geometric properties. We demonstrate the model's effectiveness across a range of geometric datasets, achieving state-of-the-art predictive performance in several benchmark scenarios. The core mechanism centers on the synergistic interplay between these two computational paradigms, leading to enhanced predictive capabilities compared to traditional methods.

title: 基于量子纠缠的模式识别算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel pattern recognition algorithm leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The algorithm utilizes a quantum entanglement-based processing framework to enhance pattern identification and classification, specifically designed to effectively handle complex patterns often found within data. Traditional pattern recognition methods can be susceptible to noise, making them suboptimal for intricate datasets. Our proposed approach aims to overcome these limitations by exploiting the correlated nature of entangled particles, offering a potential paradigm shift in pattern analysis. The core mechanism centers around establishing and maintaining entanglement between data points, allowing for a more robust and efficient pattern recognition process. This paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying patterns within complex datasets.

title: Decoherence Times and Quantum Speed Limits in Spin-Chain Systems: A Many-Body Testbed for Energy-Time Uncertainty
abstract: Quantum speed limits (QSLs) constrain the minimum time for quantum state evolution, typically derived from energy bounds like the Margolus-Levitin (ML) and Mandelstam-Tamm (MT) relations. In open systems, decoherence—driven by environmental interactions—may impose additional constraints. This work investigates whether decoherence times fundamentally limit QSLs in spin-chain systems, extending ML/MT bounds to open dynamics. By modeling spin chains with Lindblad equations and simulating Heisenberg-type interactions, we analyze the interplay between energy fluctuations, decoherence rates, and evolution times. Experimental validation via trapped-ion or superconducting-qubit arrays could test energy-time uncertainty in many-body systems. Introduction Quantum speed limits (QSLs) define the fastest possible evolution between distinguishable quantum states, critical for quantum computing and information processing. Closed-system QSLs, such as the ML [arXiv:quant-ph/9804014] and MT [DOI:10.1103/PhysRev.41.1019] bounds, rely on energy constraints. However, open systems—subject to decoherence—require extended frameworks. Decoherence times, governed by environmental couplings, may impose additional QSLs, yet their interplay with ML/MT bounds remains unexplored. Spin chains, realizable in trapped ions [DOI:10.1038/s41586-019-1394-6] and superconducting circuits, offer a many-body testbed for studying these effects. title: Non-linear Probability Model-Driven Natural Language Processing Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel non-linear probability model-driven natural language processing (NLP) algorithm designed to automatically adjust model parameters based on textual dynamism, thereby enhancing the accuracy of NLP systems. The core mechanism centers around the integration of a non-linear probabilistic model, allowing the system to adapt to evolving text patterns. Existing NLP approaches are largely static, failing to adequately address the inherent variability of natural language. This algorithm offers a significant improvement in accuracy and robustness by dynamically adjusting model parameters in response to text changes, leading to more accurate and reliable NLP results. This work addresses a critical challenge in NLP – the need for adaptive models – and presents a framework for automated parameter adjustment, paving the way for more sophisticated and versatile NLP applications.

title: Bayesian Inference based on Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum computing to accelerate Bayesian inference. Traditional Bayesian inference suffers from significant computational bottlenecks, particularly in complex models with large datasets. We propose a novel approach leveraging the inherent parallelism of quantum computers to drastically reduce the time required for inference. Specifically, we design a quantum algorithm based on a parameterized quantum circuit (PQC) to perform Bayesian updating. This approach utilizes quantum superposition and interference to perform computations on multiple possibilities simultaneously. The core claim is that this method can significantly speed up Bayesian inference. We detail the mathematical formulation of the algorithm, including the quantum circuit representation and the key operations involved. The potential of this approach to overcome the limitations of classical Bayesian inference is discussed, highlighting the transformative impact of quantum computing on probabilistic reasoning and data analysis. The efficiency gains are expected to be particularly pronounced for problems where the prior distributions and the likelihood functions are highly correlated, allowing for efficient quantum interference.

title: Adaptive Multi-Level Quantum Degradation Model
abstract: Quantum degradation processes in complex systems are increasingly recognized as multi-level phenomena, deviating from traditional single-level models. This research introduces an adaptive multi-level quantum degradation model utilizing deep neural networks to capture the intricate dynamics of quantum system decay across multiple levels. The core claim posits that quantum degradation is not a singular event but a coordinated effect of multiple levels. The proposed model dynamically adjusts its parameters based on learned features, simulating the system's evolution over various timescales. The key mechanism involves training a deep neural network to identify and characterize degradation features at each level. The model's output, represented as (Qt), reflects the quantum state at time *t*, where Qt = (q1,t, q2,t, ..., qK,t), and *K* represents the number of levels in the system. The model's adaptive nature allows it to account for the varying degrees of degradation at each level, providing a more realistic and accurate representation of quantum decay compared to conventional single-level approaches. This work addresses a critical gap in current quantum degradation modeling techniques.

title: Title: Emergent Ontology Modeling with Adaptive Topology
abstract: This paper introduces an ontology-based system for modeling emergent phenomena through dynamic topology. We propose a novel approach that constructs a 'map' of interconnected concepts, dynamically adjusting the network topology to facilitate the emergence of novel relationships and concepts. The system utilizes a topological network to represent relationships, enabling the system to explore and generate new concepts based on the existing connections. This contrasts with static ontology systems, which lack the capacity to generate new concepts organically. The core mechanism focuses on creating a 'map' – a network representation – that allows for the self-organization of concepts through connectivity. We present a preliminary implementation illustrating the system's capabilities through a simplified example, demonstrating the system's ability to generate new concepts based on initial connections.

title: Non-Von Neumann Architectures for Quantum Computing Hardware
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum computing hardware that diverges from the traditional Von Neumann architecture. The core argument centers around leveraging quantum entanglement and superposition for inherent parallel computation, addressing limitations inherent in the conventional model. We introduce a heterogeneous quantum computing architecture built upon quantum bits (qubits) and quantum circuits, designed to facilitate data processing and control through orchestrated quantum operations. The fundamental innovation lies in moving away from the sequential processing paradigm dictated by Von Neumann architecture, offering a potentially more efficient hardware platform for quantum computations. This architecture aims to unlock significant computational speedups by exploiting the quantum mechanical properties of superposition and entanglement, moving beyond the constraints of classical bit manipulation. The design incorporates a novel control system and qubit connectivity model to maximize computational parallelism. This research contributes to the exploration of alternative hardware designs critical for the advancement of scalable and performant quantum computing systems.

title: Title: Holistic Information Encryption (HIE)
abstract: This paper explores the potential of Holistic Information Encryption (HIE), a novel cryptographic system predicated on the assumption that information possesses inherent structure. Traditional cryptographic methods often rely on complex mathematical algorithms, but HIE seeks to exploit this structure for enhanced security. The core of HIE lies in the implementation of a 'Dynamic Graph Embedding' technique, which constructs a dynamic representation of the information's structure, rendering it significantly more resistant to reverse engineering. The paper will detail the design and implementation of this algorithm, discussing its potential benefits and limitations, and ultimately, will present a preliminary assessment of its security properties. The paper will conclude with a discussion of future research directions, including exploring the scalability and application of this technique to different types of information.

title: Information-Theoretic Validation of Neural Network Representations
abstract: Evaluating the quality of learned representations within neural networks remains a significant challenge. Traditional methods often rely on task-specific performance, which can be misleading and doesn't directly address the fundamental question of how well a representation captures underlying structure in the data. This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network representation validation based on information theory. We introduce a framework utilizing concepts like mutual information and transfer entropy to quantify the predictive power and representational capacity of features extracted by a neural network. These metrics provide a statistically grounded method for comparing different architectures and understanding the information content they encode. The core claim is that current methods lack a rigorous information-theoretic foundation. This work contributes a new, objective metric for assessing neural network representations, moving beyond subjective evaluations and offering concrete statistical insights.

title: Multi-Scale Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel architecture for Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) designed to effectively handle multi-scale spatio-temporal data. The core concept revolves around decomposing time-series data into multiple scales, each represented by a corresponding graph structure. A GNN is then employed to learn dependencies within these individual scales, and finally, these graph representations are fused to achieve comprehensive modeling of complex spatio-temporal phenomena. The proposed approach addresses the limitations of traditional GNNs when dealing with large-scale, multi-scale data, offering improved capabilities for capturing intricate relationships. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework through a theoretical analysis, highlighting its advantages over existing methods. The key innovation lies in the hierarchical graph representation and the subsequent integrated learning process, leading to enhanced performance in capturing temporal dynamics and spatial correlations. This work provides a foundational framework for advanced spatio-temporal modeling applications.

title: Dynamic Semantic Topological Learning Network (DSTLN)
abstract: This paper introduces the Dynamic Semantic Topological Learning Network (DSTLN), a novel deep learning architecture designed to automatically learn and adapt network semantic structures by mimicking the dynamic connectivity and plasticity observed in biological neural networks. The core mechanism of DSTLN revolves around proxy nodes, each equipped with a semantic perception module and a connection strength regulation module. These modules, operating in conjunction with information exchange and competitive learning, enable the network to dynamically construct and evolve a topology that accurately reflects the underlying semantic relationships within the data. The semantic perception module utilizes an attention mechanism for encoding input data and identifying semantic information. Subsequently, the connection strength regulation module adjusts the connection strengths between nodes based on semantic similarity and the nodes' perception of the current network state, resulting in a dynamic topology that adapts over time. The proposed DSTLN offers a promising approach to enhance the robustness and generalization capabilities of deep learning models, particularly when dealing with complex and evolving datasets. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adaptation of the network topology, a feature previously absent in traditional deep learning architectures.

title: Dynamic Quantum Error Correction Code Adaptive Design
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to designing quantum error correction (QEC) codes utilizing machine learning. The core concept involves constructing an optimization model for QEC codes and employing machine learning algorithms to dynamically adjust the code's parameters based on observed decoherence rates within the qubits. Traditional QEC code design relies heavily on theoretical analysis, often lacking the adaptability required for real-world quantum systems. This proposed method addresses this limitation by introducing a learning-based system capable of self-optimization, ultimately aiming to enhance error correction capabilities. The system learns from the specific characteristics of the quantum hardware and can adapt to changing conditions, a critical step towards practical quantum computation. The primary goal is to create a system that automatically adjusts its parameters to maximize error correction performance, paving the way for more robust and reliable quantum computations. The system's efficacy is dependent on accurate measurement of decoherence and the effectiveness of the chosen machine learning algorithm.

title: A transformer-based multi-modal fusion framework for laryngeal lesion classification using contact endoscopy
abstract: Purpose This study introduces a novel multi-modal transformer-based framework that integrates clinical data, radiomic features, and deep learning representations for automated classification of laryngeal lesions from contact endoscopy images. Methods We retrospectively enrolled 300 patients with laryngeal lesions from three independent medical centers (Centers A, B, and C), acquiring 7,847 contact endoscopy images with narrow band imaging. Clinical variables (18 features), radiomic features extracted using PyRadiomics (156 features), and deep learning representations from three state-of-the-art architectures, ConvNeXt V2, Swin Transformer V2, and EfficientNet V2 (3,328 combined features), were systematically integrated through a six-layer transformer encoder with multi-head cross-attention mechanisms. We evaluated three feature selection strategies (LASSO, mutual information, ReliefF) and three advanced classification architectures (Vision Transformer, Attention-MLP, Graph Neural Network). The framework was developed using data from Centers A and B ( n = 230 patients) with rigorous five-fold cross-validation, and validated on an independent external test set from Center C ( n = 70 patients). Results The optimal configuration (LASSO feature selection with Vision Transformer classifier) achieved accuracy of 96.1 ± 1.0% (AUC-ROC: 0.992 ± 0.007) on training, 93.8 ± 1.4% (AUC-ROC: 0.981 ± 0.012) on internal validation, and 91.4 ± 2.1% (AUC-ROC: 0.967 ± 0.019) on external testing, with sensitivity of 90.0 ± 2.8% and specificity of 92.5 ± 2.5% on the external cohort. The multi-modal fusion approach significantly outperformed all single-modality Methods clinical features alone (71.3% validation accuracy), radiomic features alone (84.2%), and the best individual deep learning model (87.6%), with improvements of 22.5, 9.6, and 6.2 percentage points respectively (all p < 0.001. Attention mechanism analysis revealed that the model dynamically weighted modality contributions, allocating 47.0% attention to deep features, 34.7% to radiomic features, and 18.3% attention to clinical features for correctly classified malignant cases. Conclusion This study presents the first comprehensive framework for laryngeal lesion classification that systematically integrates clinical data, radiomics, and deep learning through transformer-based fusion.

title: "FedWave: Code and Evaluation Logs for Stealthy Wavelet-Domain Backdoor Attacks in Federated Learning"
abstract: "This dataset contains the source code and evaluation logs supporting the manuscript \"FedWave: Stealthy Wavelet-Domain Backdoor Attacks in Federated Learning,\" submitted to the IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security.FedWave is an anchor-aligned wavelet-subband backdoor framework for federated learning (FL). It combines three mechanisms: (i) frequency-domain trigger embedding in the LH\/HL\/HH subbands of a one-level 2D Haar DWT, restricted to the blue channel for visual stealth; (ii) subband-wise trigger decomposition with probabilistic cross-client association, governed by an association probability p; and (iii) Anchor-Based Projection (ABP), which aligns each poisoned update to a safety band centred on a locally simulated, same-round benign update norm.The release includes the FedWave implementation, the baseline attack implementations used for comparison (BadNets, DBA, FIBA-FL, Neurotoxin), the evaluation harness for the nine defenses studied in the manuscript, and the per-round metric logs from which every table and figure is produced. All experiments use ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 and GTSRB and a lightweight SimpleCNN on EMNIST, under Dirichlet non-IID client partitioning.The input datasets (CIFAR-10, GTSRB, EMNIST) are third-party public resources and are NOT redistributed here; links to their official sources are provided under Links. These artifacts are released to support reproducibility and follow-on defense research. See README for responsible-use terms. "

title: Algebraic Operator Decomposition: A Partitioned Architecture for Noise-Resilient Quantum Computing
abstract: We present an operator-decomposition architecture that mathematically maps a global operator into independently executable local operators, reducing the maximum quantum circuit depth at the cost of classical reconstruction and sampling overhead. By framing complex Quantum Circuits around an operator in a vector space that can be algebraically pre-decomposed, AOD complements quantum error correction and error-mitigation approaches by performing algebraic decomposition before quantum execution. Our approach leans in the computer science definition of a Monoid: a design pattern and mathematical concept consisting of a data type, a combining function that is associative, and a safe identity (neutral) element that does not change other values when combined. Simulation wise we define a MapReduce programming model where the addition (+) is the reducer, thus leveraging a naturally stable commutative monoid which carries zero "negative-probability tax" or phase conflicts. Furthermore, we define a Vector Space of Linear Operators over Additive Abelian Groups that benefit from this paradigm, including: Inner Products, Series expansions, Traces and Convolutions. Finally, we present the mathematical foundations and simulation results for this paradigm.

title: RARF: Region-Aware Rectified Flows for 3D Brain MRI Inpainting
abstract: Medical image inpainting has the potential to improve automated brain MRI analysis by reconstructing healthy tissue within pathological regions. We introduce RARF, a task-agnostic region-aware rectified flow framework for masked data generation. We instantiate the framework for 3D brain MRI inpainting as our submission to the BraTS Inpainting Challenge 2026. RARF restricts the stochastic interpolation process to the inpainting region, while the observed voxels remain fixed and provide patient-specific anatomical context. A three-dimensional neural network receives the partially voided image, with Gaussian noise filling the missing region, together with the inpainting mask and the corresponding timestep. The model is trained using masked flow-matching and reconstruction-consistency objectives, combined with mask-aware preprocessing and data augmentation. During inference, the learned velocity field transports the initial noise toward a plausible reconstruction of the missing tissue, which is then combined with the unchanged observed anatomy. Experiments under the BraTS evaluation protocol show that the proposed approach produces competitive reconstructions while maintaining anatomical consistency. Source code is available at: https://github.com/TomasGuija/rarf.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Neural Network Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic adaptive neural network optimization algorithm designed to enhance model generalization by dynamically adjusting network parameters based on training data. Traditional neural network optimization methods often rely on static learning rates, which can lead to suboptimal performance when data shifts significantly. Our proposed algorithm incorporates a "dynamic learning rate" mechanism, allowing the network to adapt its learning rate during training to effectively navigate the data landscape and prevent local optima. The core mechanism leverages a feedback loop based on data distribution to dynamically adjust parameters, resulting in improved generalization capabilities. We present a comprehensive analysis and evaluation demonstrating the effectiveness of this algorithm compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.
