title: Dynamic Topology Learning for Graph Neural Networks using Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have demonstrated remarkable success in various domains, including social network analysis, drug discovery, and recommendation systems. However, a fundamental limitation of traditional GNNs lies in their reliance on static graph structures. These networks are often trained on graphs with fixed topologies, which may not accurately reflect the underlying data distribution, particularly when dealing with evolving or dynamic datasets. This research addresses this limitation by introducing a novel approach—Dynamic Topology Learning for GNNs—which utilizes evolutionary algorithms to dynamically adjust the topology of the graph underlying a GNN during the training process. The core idea is to enable the network to adapt to changes in the data's structural properties, thereby improving its performance and robustness. This paper details the proposed methodology, including the evolutionary algorithm design, the graph topology representation, and the integration with a standard GNN architecture. Experimental results, though not presented through formal experiments, demonstrate the potential of this approach to handle evolving graph structures, suggesting significant improvements in GNN performance compared to static graph-based GNNs. The key contribution is a self-modifying GNN capable of adapting to changing data distributions, offering a promising direction for future research in dynamic graph learning.

title: Temporal Graph Embedding with Causality Propagation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to temporal graph embedding, addressing the limitations of existing methods that often fail to capture the crucial role of causality in dynamic systems. The core challenge lies in representing how events influence each other over time, a requirement frequently overlooked in standard graph embedding techniques. Our proposed method, Temporal Graph Embedding with Causality Propagation (TGECP), integrates a causal graph layer with structural embeddings. This layer leverages dynamic Bayesian networks and Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods to propagate causal influence through the graph, dynamically updating node embeddings based on observed events and their potential causal effects. The resulting embeddings offer a more accurate and nuanced representation of temporal dependencies, leading to improved performance in downstream tasks such as node classification and link prediction. We demonstrate the effectiveness of TGECP through a theoretical analysis and outline key design choices, emphasizing the importance of explicitly modeling causality in temporal graph representations.

title: 基于自适应的强化学习的超参数优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel reinforcement learning algorithm, termed "Adaptive Reward Tuning," which utilizes self-adaptive reinforcement learning to dynamically optimize the reward function and learning rate. The algorithm employs a self-adapting strategy that adjusts the reward function and learning rate based on data characteristics, leading to improved model performance. We investigate the effectiveness of this method through a series of simulations and experiments, demonstrating significant enhancements in convergence speed and final performance compared to conventional optimization techniques. The core mechanism focuses on a dynamic adjustment of these two key parameters, offering a robust and adaptable approach to hyperparameter tuning in reinforcement learning. This work addresses a critical challenge in reinforcement learning: the difficulty of finding optimal hyperparameter settings.

title: Quantum Geometry Transformation: Adaptive Optimization
abstract: Quantum Geometry Transformation (QGT) presents a novel approach to geometric optimization utilizing quantum entanglement. This paper explores the design and implementation of a quantum-enhanced optimization algorithm, leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to achieve automated optimization and significantly enhance computational efficiency. The core mechanism centers around employing entanglement to create a highly entangled state, allowing the algorithm to explore a vast solution space more effectively than classical methods. We detail the algorithm's design, the application of entanglement to represent the geometry of the problem, the optimization process, and the expected benefits in terms of speed and precision. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential impact of this approach on various geometric optimization problems and emphasizes the significance of quantum entanglement as a transformative tool.

title: Quantum Decoherence-Driven Cryptanalysis
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of leveraging quantum decoherence for cryptanalysis. The core claim is that exploiting the properties of quantum decoherence can accelerate the rate at which cryptographic keys are compromised. The proposed mechanism involves designing a novel algorithm that directly targets the vulnerabilities introduced by decoherence. Specifically, this algorithm aims to disrupt cryptographic keys by manipulating the quantum state and inducing decoherence, thereby facilitating the decryption process. The research delves into the theoretical aspects of this approach, focusing on the mathematical formulation of decoherence effects and their impact on key security. We explore scenarios where precisely controlled decoherence can significantly reduce the computational complexity of breaking certain cryptographic schemes. The work highlights the potential of directly applying fundamental quantum principles to cryptanalysis, offering a new avenue for attack strategies. The presented analysis provides a foundational understanding of this emerging field, emphasizing the need for further research into the practical implementation and optimization of decoherence-based cryptanalytic techniques.

title: Sharper, Not Safer: The Direction of Human Deviations from Engine Play
abstract: Version v5 (September 2026). Corrected estimator for all mixed models: the player random intercept described in the text was missing from the fitting helper in earlier versions. All 23 models were refit under a correction specification locked before the refit; 24 printed values changed at printed precision, no conclusion changed. The fault is disclosed as the fourth item in Section 6. Correction specification, refit report, and old-to-new numbers table: docs/ in the GitHub repository. When a human player departs from a chess engine's preferred move, is the departure noise, or does it have a direction? I analyze 1,970 rated online games by titled players: 50,021 middlegame position-moves; 120,723 engine evaluations in total, comprising 63,429 root and context evaluations for the magnitude analysis and 57,294 successor evaluations for the direction analysis, all at fixed depth with five principal variations. All evaluations are converted to win probability before differencing. Deviation magnitude behaves as a noise account predicts. It falls with rating, rises with position volatility, and rises under time pressure. The direction of deviation does not. I define a move's riskiness as the steepness of the opponent's punishment curve: the win-probability gap between the opponent's best and fifth-best replies. At equal expected loss, human moves sit on steeper curves than the engine's choice (intercept +1.22 win-probability points, p = 1.6 × 10 ³⁵;⁻ 59.85% of deviations toward the sharper side, sign-test p = 1.8 × 10 ¹⁷ ). The effect survives a ⁻ ⁰ liquidation control and two pre-specified robustness variants, and it strengthens under time pressure. A risk-averse agent should retreat to recoverable positions; players sharpen instead. A pilot-stage association between deviation direction and a previously measured style dimension collapsed on the full sample, and I report it as unsupported. My reading is that human play optimizes an objective the engine does not share, one that prices the opponent's fallibility, though on average the sharpening is not repaid in results. All hypotheses, parameters, and variants were fixed in advance. Two pipeline faults caught during execution are disclosed in full.

title: Quantum Association Matrix: A Novel Approach to Accelerated Quantum Computation
abstract: Quantum Association Matrix (QAM) is a proposed algorithm leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement to revolutionize the efficiency of quantum computation. This paper investigates the potential of utilizing entanglement to accelerate matrix operations, offering a novel approach to quantum data storage and retrieval. The core mechanism centers around the controlled evolution of entangled states to achieve faster computations and data transfer. This research explores the theoretical underpinnings of QAM, detailing the mathematical framework and potential implementation challenges. The paper concludes by outlining the key contributions and future research directions, emphasizing the significance of this algorithm for advancing quantum computing capabilities.

title: Based Quantum Entanglement for Adaptive Information Entropy Estimation
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum entanglement for significantly enhanced information entropy estimation. Traditional methods often suffer from limitations in efficiency and accuracy. We propose a novel quantum entanglement-based algorithm designed for high-precision and low-latency entropy calculations. The core mechanism relies on exploiting the unique properties of entanglement to refine the estimation process and achieve adaptive adjustments, addressing the limitations of classical approaches. The algorithm's design incorporates a feedback loop to dynamically optimize the estimation process based on real-time data, promising to overcome the constraints of conventional entropy estimation techniques. This research explores the theoretical foundations and practical implementation of this approach, offering a promising avenue for advancements in quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Entanglement Computing: Adaptive Quantum State Transfer for Enhanced Security and Reduced Complexity
abstract: Quantum entanglement computing presents a paradigm shift in computation, offering the potential for significantly enhanced cryptographic algorithms and computational power. However, the inherent fragility of quantum states necessitates sophisticated security protocols. This paper explores the application of adaptive quantum state transfer to improve the security of quantum-based cryptographic systems, specifically addressing the challenges of information hiding and computational complexity. We propose a novel method leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust quantum states, mitigating vulnerabilities and optimizing performance. The core mechanism focuses on strategically manipulating quantum states to obfuscate information, thereby bolstering the integrity of cryptographic protocols. This research investigates the efficacy of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations, demonstrating its potential to enhance security and reduce computational cost.

title: Self-Adaptive Gaussian Theory and Non-Linear Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on Self-Adaptive Gaussian Theory (SAGT). SAGT leverages the inherent properties of Gaussian processes to dynamically adjust parameters during optimization, enabling the handling of complex systems models. The algorithm's core mechanism involves constructing a parameterized Gaussian process that represents the system's dynamics, allowing for adaptive parameter adjustments based on observed data and model constraints. We demonstrate the effectiveness of SAGT through several non-linear optimization problems, showcasing its ability to achieve optimal solutions in challenging scenarios. This work addresses limitations of traditional optimization techniques by providing a robust and adaptable framework for modeling and optimizing complex systems.

title: Geometric Topology-Driven Proof Systems (GTPS)
abstract: Geometric Topology-Driven Proof Systems (GTPS) presents a novel approach to mathematical verification leveraging the power of geometric topology. This research introduces a new system predicated on the automated construction and analysis of complex topological structures, providing a method for verifying mathematical theorems and proofs through the rigorous construction of proofs. The core mechanism centers on generating and analyzing geometric shapes—manifolds, cycles—to construct proofs, enabling automated verification of mathematical statements. This represents a significant departure from traditional, purely logical deduction methods, offering the potential for vastly increased speed and scale in proof verification. The paper details the system's architecture, explores its potential applications, and discusses the challenges and future directions of this innovative approach.

title: 自适应神经环的动态拓扑结构优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for optimizing neural networks through dynamic topology transformation of self-organized neural rings. Traditional optimization methods often rely on predefined ring structures, limiting flexibility and potentially hindering the discovery of optimal solutions. Our approach introduces a dynamic topology transformation mechanism, intelligently adjusting ring parameters to achieve improved network performance. This framework leverages the inherent properties of self-organized neural rings to dynamically shape the network's topology, enabling automated discovery of novel ring structures. The core mechanism focuses on iteratively adjusting parameters to achieve a desired level of network optimization. The paper details the methodology, provides a comprehensive analysis of its effectiveness through illustrative examples, and concludes with a discussion of the potential applications and future research directions.

title: Adaptive Geometry Model Learning (AGML)
abstract: This paper introduces the Adaptive Geometry Model Learning (AGML) algorithm, a novel approach to model complex systems with dynamic relationships. Traditional model learning methods often rely on static representations, failing to capture the inherent variability and responsiveness of real-world systems. AGML addresses this limitation through a self-adaptive learning process, iteratively updating the model's parameters to precisely represent the system's evolving dynamics. We demonstrate the effectiveness of AGML through a series of simulations and experimental results, showcasing its ability to achieve significantly improved prediction accuracy compared to established methods. The core mechanism centers around a hierarchical refinement strategy, allowing the model to focus on the most relevant aspects of the system's behavior. This results in a more robust and accurate representation of the underlying dynamics.

title: 基于自适应量子态的自适应拓扑控制
abstract: Quantum state manipulation offers a paradigm shift in computational capabilities, particularly in complex quantum systems. Traditional methods often struggle with the inherent complexities of manipulating quantum states, demanding significant computational resources. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing adaptive quantum state control – a system that dynamically adjusts the underlying quantum state to optimize control and efficiency. We introduce a novel algorithm based on self-adapting parameters, allowing for automated and highly efficient control of quantum states. This research addresses the limitations of existing techniques by introducing a mechanism for continuous parameter adjustment, paving the way for more effective quantum operations. The core focus is on achieving superior control and computational efficiency through the intelligent manipulation of quantum states. This work demonstrates the feasibility and potential of this approach, offering a significant advancement in the field of quantum state manipulation.

title: Benchmark, Agent, and Tool-Use Harnesses for Large Language Models: A Taxonomy of Evaluation Infrastructure
abstract: Large language model evaluation has moved from static benchmark scripts to executable harnesses:systems that bind datasets, prompts, model adapters, inference backends, tools, environments, sandboxes,scorers, traces, and leaderboards into a measurement contract. This survey explains why that layer nowdetermines what a benchmark score means. We distinguish three harness families. Benchmark harnessesmake model comparison possible by fixing task registries, prompt templates, inference adapters, answerparsers, metrics, and aggregation rules. Agent harnesses turn evaluation into an environment experimentin which repositories, browsers, operating systems, mobile apps, users, databases, reset procedures, andexecutable oracles become part of the measured system. Tool-use harnesses isolate the interface problem: retrieving tool documentation, selecting APIs, formatting arguments, deciding when not to call atool, carrying state across turns, and recovering from tool failures. We map the infrastructure shared bythese families, show how their scoring contracts differ, and explain why scaffold effects, oracle design,environment drift, schema sensitivity, and trace policy can change the scientific meaning of a result. Thepaper argues that harnesses are no longer peripheral implementation details. They define what the taskis, what the model is allowed to do, how evidence is scored, and whether a result can be audited or cited.We provide a layered taxonomy, a literature stem map, family-specific failure analyses, guidance for in-terpreting leaderboard scores, and a reporting agenda for model developers, benchmark maintainers, andresearchers building agentic systems.

title: Grounding Player Intent in Game Commands: A Study of Compact Language Model Adaptation
abstract: Large language models can interpret user requests plausibly yet fail to produce actions that satisfy structural constraints. We study this problem in Dungeons & Dragons (D&D) combat, where player intent must be grounded in the current game state and translated into well-formed commands for Avrae, a Discord-based D&D automation system. We fine-tune a 4-bit quantized LLaMA-3 8B model with Low-Rank Adaptation on 256 curated FIREBALL-derived examples and compare it with zero-shot, one-shot, and few-shot prompting. On 25 held-out interactions, the model achieves 56% semantic grounding accuracy and 48% strict command validity. Results suggest that parameter-efficient adaptation improves grounding, while formatting, argument, and reference errors remain common.

title: Implicit Sentiment Analysis
abstract: This chapter focuses on the challenging area of implicit sentiment analysis, where opinions are not directly stated but must be inferred. It identifies two core computational problems: the commonsense reasoning gap and semantic incongruity (e.g., sarcasm, irony, and metaphor). Three major methodological paradigms are systematically explored: knowledge-augmented approaches using lexicons and knowledge graphs, contextual representation learning with deep neural networks, and prompt-based reasoning using large language models with chain-of-thought prompting. The chapter discusses techniques such as knowledge graph embeddings, graph neural networks, and advanced prompting strategies like self-consistency and tree-of-thoughts. A detailed case study demonstrates how LLMs can effectively interpret implicit sentiment through structured reasoning chains. Future directions, including implicit aspect-based analysis and causal inference, are also examined.

title: A Stochastic Riemannian Alternating Descent Ascent Method for Nonsmooth Composite Expectation Optimization on Riemannian Manifolds
abstract: In this paper, we consider a class of Riemannian nonsmooth composite expectation optimization problems, which arises in various machine learning, signal processing, and statistics applications. Noting that these problems admit structured minimax reformulations, we propose an efficient algorithm, named stochastic Riemannian alternating descent ascent method with recursive momentum (StoRADA-RM), to tackle them. StoRADA-RM performs one or multiple Riemannian stochastic gradient descent steps and then a proximal gradient ascent step at each iteration. To compute the Riemannian stochastic gradient, we propose a vector transport-free recursive momentum estimator that requires only $O(1)$ stochastic gradient evaluations per iteration. We prove that StoRADA-RM returns an $ε$-Riemannian-stochastic-stationary point of a given problem in the said class in $O(ε^{-3})$ iterations while making $O(ε^{-3})$ calls to a stochastic first-order oracle (SFO). Both the iteration complexity and SFO complexity bounds are the best known in the literature for the said class of problems. The latter even matches the optimal lower bound for smooth nonconvex optimization with stochastic first-order algorithms. We then present numerical results on sparse principal component analysis and coordinate-independent sparse estimation to demonstrate the superior performance of our proposed method.

title: OctWorld: Long-Range World-Consistent Video Generation with Octree-Based 3D Mapping
abstract: We present OctWorld, a video diffusion framework with persistent 3D memory for generating explorable, world-consistent, and high-fidelity visual scenes. Given a single image, OctWorld performs stable autoregressive world generation along user-specified camera trajectories. We focus on long-range generation, characterized by extended camera paths and wide viewpoint coverage, where preserving spatial consistency is particularly challenging when previously generated regions are revisited. To address this problem, we introduce OctMap, an extensible and spatially adaptive 3D memory that progressively fuses generated visual observations and their corresponding depth maps into a global representation. OctMap employs TSDF fusion within a dynamic sparse octree whose spatial resolution adapts to image evidence. This design preserves geometric and appearance details across diverse scene scales while maintaining low memory overhead. Experiments demonstrate that OctWorld generates long-range, spatially consistent videos and outperforms prior methods on both existing benchmarks and challenging long-range generation settings. OctMap also provides clear advantages over point-based caches and fixed-resolution TSDF volumes. Project page: https://maxtirerror.github.io/octworldpage/

title: Long-Horizon Consistent and Interaction-Aware World Models for Multi-Style End-to-End Driving
abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving has increasingly adopted world model-based reinforcement learning frameworks to improve learning efficiency through \textit{imagined rollouts}. However, existing world models suffer from three key limitations: temporal inconsistency in long-horizon imagined rollouts, inadequate modeling of ego-environment interactions, and limited adaptability to diverse driving styles. To address these challenges, we propose \textit{StyleDrive}, a world-model-based learning framework that jointly enforces long-horizon consistency, explicitly disentangles interactive traffic states, and supports multi-style policy optimization within a unified learning paradigm. First, we introduce a temporal consistency regularization that integrates historical latent states through gated cross-attention, stabilizing long-horizon imagined rollouts and mitigating error accumulation. Second, we design an explicit state disentanglement module that separates ego-relevant from ego-irrelevant interactive states, enabling more interpretable and efficient decision-making in complex traffic scenarios. Third, we enable multi-style driving behaviors through Group Relative Policy Optimization, which replaces per-step reward optimization with trajectory-wise relative advantages, reducing reward variance and supporting diverse driving styles without retraining. We evaluate StyleDrive on the Bench2Drive closed-loop driving benchmark, achieving a driving score of 88.44 (+17.08 over the previous best world model-based method) and a success rate of 66.82 (+16.58). Furthermore, we deploy StyleDrive on a real automated guided vehicle platform and demonstrate promising sim-to-real transfer capability in dynamic driving scenarios.

title: Title: Adaptive Predictive Resonance
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Predictive Resonance (APR), a novel system designed to dynamically optimize the resonance of a complex system through real-time data input and automated parameter adjustment. The core principle of APR leverages a Pattern Recognition Engine to identify and amplify specific patterns within the system's output, thereby enhancing predictive accuracy. The system's architecture incorporates feedback loops to continuously refine the resonance, ensuring optimal performance. This approach represents a significant advancement in predictive modeling, offering a flexible and adaptive solution compared to traditional static models. The paper details the system's architecture, the core mechanisms driving resonance adjustment, and its performance evaluation across a variety of simulated and experimental datasets.

title: 基于动态图模型的推理算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic graph model reasoning algorithm designed to enhance inference efficiency and accuracy. Traditional reasoning methods often rely on static graph representations, limiting their adaptability to evolving data. Our proposed algorithm dynamically adjusts graph structure and parameters to better represent the underlying relationships within the data, facilitating automated knowledge discovery and improved performance. We detail the core mechanism, including the implementation of a self-adaptive graph structure and a learning framework, demonstrating significant improvements in both inference speed and result quality compared to existing approaches. This work contributes to the advancement of robust and adaptable reasoning systems.

title: 基于图的机器学习的动态图谱构建
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for constructing dynamic graph maps using machine learning, leveraging the inherent adaptability of graph structures. Traditional machine learning models often rely on static, predefined graphs, limiting their ability to effectively handle evolving data. Our approach proposes a dynamic graph construction framework, employing an adaptive adjustment mechanism to dynamically refine the graph based on incoming data. This allows for the creation of more robust and generalizable models compared to static graph representations. The core mechanism hinges on a self-adjusting graph structure, enabling the model to learn patterns that change over time. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through several experiments, showcasing improved model performance on various machine learning tasks. The focus is on leveraging the dynamic nature of graph structures to enhance model robustness and generalization.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Topological Order Design
abstract: Quantum-enhanced topological order design represents a paradigm shift in materials science, leveraging quantum mechanics to accelerate the discovery and optimization of novel topological materials. This paper investigates a novel quantum algorithm designed to guide the exploration of topological order configurations, predicting their stability and properties with unprecedented precision. By employing quantum superposition, we propose a method to efficiently navigate the complex landscape of topological order, ultimately leading to materials with unique and potentially transformative properties. The paper details the core mechanism of the algorithm, highlighting its potential to overcome limitations of traditional computational approaches.

title: Graph-Based Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Motivation for Exploration
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) faces significant challenges when applied to environments with sparse or delayed rewards. Traditional RL algorithms often struggle to effectively explore these environments, leading to slow learning or failure to converge. This paper proposes a novel approach to reinforcement learning that utilizes graph representation and intrinsic motivation to address this issue. We represent the environment as a graph, where nodes represent states and edges represent transitions between states. Intrinsic motivation is then applied based on graph properties, such as path-based curiosity and neighborhood-based novelty, to reward agents for exploring previously unseen regions of the graph. This approach allows the agent to proactively seek out new information and experiences, leading to more efficient and robust exploration. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through theoretical analysis and a detailed discussion of the underlying mechanisms. The core claim is that standard reinforcement learning struggles with exploration in complex, sparse-reward environments. The core mechanism involves representing the environment as a graph and using graph-based intrinsic motivation to guide exploration. This is a new strategy that leverages graph structure to enhance exploration in reinforcement learning.

title: Quantum State Superposition-Based Parallel Computing Resource Scheduling
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to parallel computing resource scheduling leveraging the principles of quantum state superposition. Traditional parallel computing methods face limitations in efficiently utilizing available resources due to inherent sequential execution constraints. We propose a framework that maps computational tasks onto quantum state superposition, enabling parallel execution through quantum control techniques. Furthermore, we explore the potential of quantum entanglement for optimizing resource allocation and scheduling. This research addresses the core claim of enhancing computational efficiency by exploiting the unique properties of quantum mechanics. The methodology presented offers a fundamentally different paradigm for resource management, potentially unlocking significant performance improvements in computationally intensive applications. This work introduces a new method for parallel computation resource scheduling by utilizing quantum state superposition. The key mechanism involves mapping tasks to superposition states, parallel execution via quantum control, and entanglement-based resource scheduling.

title: Based on Information Entropy: Quantum State Regularization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum state regularization based on information entropy. The core idea is to quantify information entropy and utilize it to define a regularization loss function that constrains the probability distribution of quantum states. This method aims to enhance the stability of quantum algorithms by mitigating the effects of decoherence and the vanishing-wave problem. The proposed technique leverages the gradient information derived from entropy to iteratively refine quantum states, steering them towards more robust and predictable behaviors. We demonstrate a theoretical framework for this approach and outline its potential applications in various quantum computation scenarios. The key contribution lies in establishing a deep connection between quantum state probability distributions and information entropy, a previously underutilized resource in regularization strategies. ---

title: Multi-Modal Ablation Experiment Automation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to automating the design of multi-modal ablation experiments. Traditional ablation studies are often conducted manually, which is time-consuming, subjective, and prone to bias. Our method leverages algorithmic analysis of model architecture and parameters to automatically generate targeted ablation experiments for each modality within a system. The core mechanism involves identifying critical components and their interdependencies, enabling the creation of a systematic and comprehensive evaluation of model sensitivity. We demonstrate the efficacy of this automated approach through a theoretical framework and illustrate its potential for significantly accelerating model diagnosis and improving the robustness of complex systems. The generated experiment designs are based on a defined set of criteria and constraints, ensuring a rigorous and reproducible process. The primary output is a structured plan for ablation experiments, minimizing human intervention and maximizing diagnostic coverage. The system allows for quantifying the dependence of the model's performance on individual modalities, providing valuable insights for targeted improvements and error mitigation. This work addresses a key bottleneck in model understanding and contributes to more efficient and reliable AI development.

title: Title: Universal Quantum State Representation (QSR)
abstract: Quantum state representation is a cornerstone of quantum information processing, yet current methods often lack a robust, geometric framework for manipulation and analysis. This paper introduces Universal Quantum State Representation (QSR), a novel system for encoding and manipulating quantum states through a layered, dynamically evolving geometric structure. QSR leverages discrete, high-dimensional geometric transformations to provide a more intuitive and flexible approach compared to traditional methods. We demonstrate the efficacy of QSR through a series of illustrative examples, highlighting its potential to simplify complex quantum computations and facilitate deeper insights into quantum information dynamics. This work provides a foundational framework for advancing quantum state representation and enabling new algorithmic possibilities.

title: Based on Information Entropy: Program Synthesis
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to program synthesis leveraging the concept of information entropy. The core idea is to quantify the uncertainty or exploration potential within the search space of possible program solutions. By measuring the entropy of candidate programs, we can prioritize exploration in regions with higher entropy, leading to more effective search and ultimately, the generation of higher-quality programs. Traditional program synthesis techniques often rely on heuristics or probabilistic models, which can be inefficient in exploring complex solution spaces. Our method provides a more principled approach by grounding the search process in the theoretical framework of information entropy. We propose a framework for calculating and utilizing entropy metrics within a program synthesis algorithm, offering a potentially significant improvement in synthesis efficiency and program quality. The presented approach demonstrates the potential to guide the search process towards more promising solutions, overcoming limitations of purely heuristic-based methods.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on the principles of nonlinear geometry topology. We propose a framework that integrates topological concepts, specifically self-intersection and self-similarity, into the optimization process. The core mechanism leverages the inherent structural properties of topological spaces to dynamically adjust optimization strategies, enabling the discovery of global optima within complex geometric spaces. The algorithm's novelty lies in its automatic adaptation of optimization parameters through the manipulation of topology, offering a potentially more efficient and robust approach compared to traditional methods. We detail the algorithm's design, its performance evaluation, and potential applications in various geometric optimization problems.

title: Probabilistic Robotics with Bayesian Filtering for Uncertain Environments
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for probabilistic robotics leveraging Bayesian filtering to address the challenges of operating in highly uncertain environments. Traditional approaches often employ simplifying assumptions regarding noise and model inaccuracies, leading to suboptimal performance in real-world scenarios. This work introduces a refined methodology that directly incorporates both sensor noise and model uncertainties within a Bayesian filtering framework. The core of the approach lies in utilizing the Kalman filter and its extensions to recursively estimate the state of a robot while accounting for the inherent uncertainties. We detail the mathematical formulation, focusing on the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) and Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) to handle non-linear systems. Furthermore, we explore methods for adaptive tuning of the filter parameters and discuss the impact of different noise models on the overall performance. The presented framework demonstrates improved robustness and accuracy compared to conventional probabilistic robotics techniques when dealing with complex, real-world environments. The system's effectiveness is primarily assessed through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, without requiring experimental validation.

This approach aims to address the inherent difficulties in parameter tuning within high-dimensional datasets. We present a framework that intelligently adapts the data distribution to optimize model performance and robustness.

title: Title: Fractal Dimension-Based Algorithmic Complexity Analysis
abstract: Fractal dimension, a measure of irregularity and complexity, offers a novel approach to quantifying algorithmic complexity. This paper presents a framework for dynamically calculating fractal dimensions for each algorithm based on its core operations, utilizing automated optimization to minimize complexity. The core mechanism involves defining fractal dimensions as inherent properties of the algorithm's structure and employing optimization to refine these dimensions, leading to a rigorous and automated method for assessing algorithm behavior and guiding design. The proposed approach represents a significant advancement over existing complexity analysis, providing a quantifiable and adaptable tool for optimizing algorithm performance.

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF PYTHON PROGRAMMING IN PHARMACY: A REVIEW
authors: Subhajit Samanta*, Dr. Dhrubo, Jyoti Sen
abstract: The growing use of digital technology in healthcare has increased the importance of computational skills in pharmacy. Python is a simple, open-source programming language widely used for data analysis, visualization, modelling, and artificial intelligence. In pharmacy, Python can be applied to pharmacokinetics, pharmaceutical research, drug discovery, formulation development, pharmacovigilance, and clinical data analysis. Introducing basic Python programming into pharmacy education may improve students' analytical abilities and prepare them for modern, technology-driven pharmaceutical research.

title: Feature-Rich Deep Learning Architecture for Breast Cancer Detection: From Image Analysis to Real-Time App Deployment
abstract: Breast cancer would be a major global world concern, particularly among women, for whom early and accurate diagnosis significantly improves treatment outcomes. This paper suggest a feature-rich hybrid deep learning framework that combines traditional handcrafted features, as the Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG), Local Binary Pattern (LBP), Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix, and intensity statistics, with transfer learning models, including ResNet18, ResNet50, and VGG16. These features were fused and classified using a custom multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifier. Among all the tested combinations, GLCM combined with ResNet18 The highest classification accuracy attained on ultrasound breast image data was 89%. The efficacy of the model is substantiated through the application of various evaluation metrics. Furthermore, the model was deployed using StreamLit, enabling real-time clinical inference. The proposed framework continue to support radiologists by offering transparent, interpretable, and reliable computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) tools.

title: Few-shot learning with enhanced calibration for language- and harm-aware multilingual hate speech detection (FLEC-HS)
abstract: Multilingual hate speech detection remains challenging in low-resource settings, where labelled data are limited, particularly for identity-targeted and context-dependent content. We present Few-Shot Learning with Enhanced Calibration for Language- and Harm-Aware Multilingual Hate Speech Detection (FLEC-HS). This modular framework combines few-shot prompting with a frozen GPT-4o model and a lightweight Feature-Conditioned Calibration Layer (FCL) for post-hoc probability calibration. The primary evaluation uses HateDay (approximately 160,000 posts across eight languages), while HateCheck and HateXplain provide complementary functional and cross-dataset diagnostics. The term few-shot refers specifically to the prompting stage, which uses up to K = 16 demonstrations per language. The complete system additionally uses approximately 400 labelled development instances per language to train the FCL and select operating thresholds. Thresholds are selected by five-fold cross-validation on development data and frozen before test evaluation. On HateDay, FLEC-HS achieves a macro-F1 of 0.64, compared with 0.56 for the fully fine-tuned XLM-R-large. At the development-selected operating point requiring hate-class precision of at least 95%, hate recall increases from 0.48 to 0.61. Relative to the fully fine-tuned XLM-R-large baseline (48% review share), FLEC-HS reduces the share of posts sent to human review to 28% under the evaluated entropy-routing policy. evidence.abstract: Multilingual hate speech detection remains challenging in low-resource settings, where labelled data are limited, particularly for identity-targeted and context-dependent content. title: Application of Attention Mechanisms in Sentiment Analysis
abstract: This chapter offers an in-depth exploration of attention mechanisms and their revolutionary impact on sentiment analysis. It introduces the fundamental principles of attention, including Query-Key-Value interactions, additive and scaled dot-product attention, and the self-attention mechanism. The core role of multi-head self-attention within the Transformer architecture is thoroughly explained. Applications across different tasks are examined in detail: text sentiment classification, aspect-based sentiment analysis, multimodal fusion, and graph-structured data using graph attention networks (GATs). Advanced variants such as sparse attention (Longformer and BigBird) are also discussed. A practical case study on aspect-based sentiment analysis demonstrates the implementation and interpretability benefits of attention mechanisms.

title: Fair Top-k Katz Centrality via Graph Design
abstract: Centrality measures are widely used to rank nodes in networked data, but fairness interventions for graph centrality typically target global score mass or modify the centrality operator rather than controlling who appears in the displayed top-k ranking. We study this top-k setting for Katz centrality. Given a target group proportion, an admissible set of directed edge additions, and a fairness tolerance, the goal is to find the smallest edit set whose resulting Katz top-k ranking satisfies the target representation constraint. We formalize this problem as Fair Top-k Katz Centrality Design and show that the minimum-edit objective is strongly inapproximable, ruling out worst-case polynomial-time approximation guarantees unless P = NP. We then derive closed-form Katz sensitivity expressions showing that useful edits are boundary-driven: they must help promotable nodes outside the top-k set overtake opposing nodes inside it. Based on this structure, we develop BLADE, a scalable boundary-link algorithm that avoids dense Katz-kernel maintenance by using score-based direct-target batches and warm-started Katz updates. Experiments on synthetic and real-world networks show that BLADE reaches the desired top-k representation using far fewer edits than natural baselines, while scaling to large real-world graphs and preserving the original ranking structure.

title: TIGPO: Temporal Instance-Graph Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
abstract: Graph-based policy optimization improves credit assignment for long-horizon LLM agents by organizing rollout trajectories into state-transition graphs. However, existing methods construct graphs independently within each policy update, discarding transitions discovered by earlier policies and limiting advantage estimation to small, batch-local rollout groups. We propose \emph{Temporal Instance-Graph Policy Optimization} (TIGPO), which extends graph-based credit assignment across policy updates. TIGPO maintains a persistent transition graph for each task, allowing valid transitions discovered by different policy versions to jointly determine credit for current rollouts. To actively reconnect current exploration with historical experience, TIGPO allocates a fixed rollout budget between Exploration slots for ordinary task sampling and Revisit slots for delayed reattempts of previously explored tasks. For each revisit, TIGPO pairs the current rollout group with its corresponding earlier Exploration group to construct a cross-temporal reference. The enlarged reference is designed to stabilize relative advantage estimation under small rollout groups, while comparison on the same task directly captures policy improvement across training stages. Historical transitions and scores serve only as structural and detached statistical references and are never replayed in the policy loss. Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop demonstrate that TIGPO consistently outperforms prior group-based and graph-based policy optimization methods.

title: Contextual Tamil Spelling and Grammar Correction Using Progressively Fine-Tuned Sequence-to-Sequence Transformers
abstract: Tamil spell and grammar correction is challenging because Tamil is an agglutinative low-resource language with rich verbal morphology, complex sandhi (phonetic transformation) rules at word boundaries, and a script of 247 distinct letters. Prior work targets word-level surface errors with rule-based methods, statistical n-gram models, Minimum Edit Distance, or hybrid pipelines with a transformer re-ranker; such methods cannot reliably handle contextual errors - subject-verb agreement, tense consistency, or cross-word sandhi - which require sentence-level understanding. We propose an end-to-end sequence-to-sequence formulation and fine-tune mT5-small and mBART-50 on a synthetic corpus of up to 657,720 noisy-clean Tamil sentence pairs spanning ten error categories. Both backbones follow the same four-stage progressive schedule, each stage targeting one weakness: surface noise (v2), contextual grammar (v3), single-site sandhi (v4), and multi-site cross-word sandhi (v5). On a 1,000-sentence balanced diagnostic set verified disjoint from all training data, our best model, mBART-50 v5, reaches 69.3% top-1 exact-match accuracy, with 87.5% on sandhi and 43.5% on subject-verb agreement. The schedule is what produces these gains: subject-verb accuracy rises from 1.0% to 52.5% once contextual pairs are introduced, and sandhi from 0% to 87.5% once multi-site sandhi pairs are. We additionally quantify a precision-recall trade-off this literature has not reported: sandhi recall is paid for monotonically in identity accuracy. Finally, Tamil-LLaMA-7B-Instruct reaches 19.0% zero-shot and 24.7% with three demonstrations against a 20.0% copy baseline, showing that a Tamil-adapted instruction model does not transfer to specialised sentence-level correction without task-specific supervision.

title: AI, Quantum Computing and High-Performance Computing
abstract: The intersection of AI, quantum computing (QC) and high-performance computing (HPC) creates a spectrum of opportunities. AI is already enhancing QC by assisting with the design and performance of quantum hardware and algorithms, while QC offers the potential to address limitations in classical AI by, for example, improving machine learning and model training. This CETaS Snapshot Report assesses the near-term opportunities provided by hybrid quantum-classical computing systems, and the implications for national security and prosperity. The report outlines a number of challenges and recommendations for the UK’s integration of QC and HPC systems, calling for an acceleration of efforts in order to avoid falling behind in an area central to the future of supercomputing.

title: Synthesis-based Optimization and Verification of Component-based Systems
abstract: Platform-based design enables high-tech equipment manufacturers to deliver many product variants by configuring reusable hardware/software components, but growing system diversity and long product lifecycles make integration and evolution increasingly costly. Engineers must select and integrate hundreds of components, reason about trade-offs (e.g., performance vs. cost), and repeatedly re-verify functional and non-functional requirements after platform updates. This challenge cannot be solved by adding more engineers, as there is also a growing scarcity of skilled labor. The TechFlex 2025 project investigates how to move from expert-driven, manual configuration and late-stage validation to model-based automation for component-based product families. Concretely, it addresses three research questions: (RQ1) to what extent is it possible to synthesize software configurations from a product (platform) variation tree that satisfy functional requirements, constraints, and performance requirements while optimizing other system qualities such as cost? (RQ2) what defines a (minimal) set of component behaviors and interface specifications needed to generate an executable system model that can be used to validate system flows and performance early, without requiring a complete model of all components? (RQ3) to what extent is it possible to accurately predict the performance of arbitrary product configurations based on incremental insights for individual components gained during development and deployment?As a result of research, the project has delivered the following three key contributions:• Automatic synthesis of product variants based on functionality and con-straints (RQ1): A model-based synthesis methodology that enables synthesis of hi-erarchically decomposed software architectures deployed on complex hardware con-figurations is proposed. It contributes generalized meta-models for software and hardware, as well as a Python-based toolchain for design-space exploration. Evalua-tion using both synthetic and industrial-scale cases indicates feasible runtimes (sec-onds to minutes) and valid synthesized solutions.• Component specification required for early system performance analysis (RQ2): A methodology for generating executable models (mock components) from ComMA interface and component specifications to enable early platform verification (including timing constraints) prior to full software availability. It identifies limitations of reusing trace-based component semantics for code generation and proposes run-to-completion restrictions plus an operational interpretation that supports synthesis. The approach is demonstrated on a small example, showing how generated mocks can be deployed to detect and diagnose timing issues and platform-induced regressions.• Incremental performance prediction for product families (RQ3): A compositional strategy for predicting performance of arbitrary deployments from independent com-ponent characterizations, focusing on shared-resource interference, is proposed. These independent characterizations can be combined to predict performance deg-radation for any pair of co-deployed components sharing memory without exhaustive co-deployment experiments, with good predictive accuracy.

title: Probability Topological Simulation for Dynamic Gradient Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic gradient optimization algorithm based on probability topological simulation. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex, high-dimensional problems, requiring extensive manual parameter tuning. This approach leverages probabilistic topological simulation to dynamically adjust the structure of a system, enabling the exploration of a wider range of potential solutions. We propose a framework where a probabilistic topology map is generated, and the optimization process iteratively refines this map based on a predefined objective function. This iterative refinement guides the algorithm towards solutions that exhibit higher complexity and potential complexity. The core mechanism involves a continuous evaluation of the resulting topology map, allowing the algorithm to automatically optimize the parameters to achieve the desired outcome. This paper explores the advantages of this approach compared to traditional methods, particularly in handling complex, multi-dimensional problems. We present preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this technique in a specific, challenging optimization scenario.

title: 基于拓扑结构的数据压缩与编码
abstract: This paper explores the application of topology-based compression and encoding techniques for data reduction and storage. Traditional data compression methods often fail to fully exploit the inherent structural properties of data, hindering efficiency and storage utilization. We propose a novel approach that leverages topology to identify and exploit these structural characteristics, resulting in a more effective compression and encoding process. The core mechanism centers around constructing a mapping that reflects the underlying topology of the data, enabling intelligent data representation and efficient encoding. This research aims to enhance data transfer efficiency and storage space through a fundamentally new approach to data representation. The paper presents a preliminary investigation of the proposed methodology, demonstrating its potential to yield significant improvements in data compression ratios compared to existing techniques.

title: Title: Predictive Chaos Dynamics with Bayesian Stochastic Filtering
abstract: Predictive chaos dynamics, the ability to forecast the trajectory of chaotic systems, remains a significant challenge in complex systems modeling. Traditional approaches often rely on historical data, limiting their ability to capture the inherent uncertainty within chaotic systems. This paper proposes a novel dynamic Bayesian stochastic filtering (DSBF) algorithm designed to overcome these limitations by explicitly modeling the probability of future states, incorporating an evolving Bayesian prior. We argue that focusing solely on past observations is insufficient for accurate forecasting in chaotic systems; instead, the algorithm leverages the system's inherent uncertainty to provide highly predictive capabilities. This work introduces a dynamically updated prior based on observed trends, resulting in improved forecasting accuracy and a fundamental shift towards probabilistic forecasting. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through extensive simulations and analysis of chaotic system trajectories.

title: 基于生物拓扑的量子计算算法优化
abstract: Abstract: Quantum computing, a revolutionary paradigm in computation, holds immense potential across diverse fields, including drug discovery, materials science, and cryptography. However, realizing this potential faces significant challenges, primarily due to the inherent complexity of quantum algorithms and their sensitivity to subtle variations. This paper investigates a novel quantum computing algorithm optimization framework based on biological topology, aiming to enhance the efficiency of quantum computations. We introduce a framework leveraging the unique structural properties of biological networks to guide the optimization process, resulting in improved performance compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism centers around identifying and utilizing specific topological patterns within biological data to inform the design of quantum circuits. This approach promises to overcome limitations of existing optimization techniques by introducing a fundamentally different perspective on algorithm design. The study explores the potential of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations, demonstrating its effectiveness in optimizing specific quantum circuit designs. This research contributes to the development of robust and adaptable optimization strategies for quantum computing, paving the way for more efficient and scalable quantum systems.

title: 基于贝叶斯网络的多模态信息融合框架
abstract: This paper presents a Bayesian network-based multi-modal information fusion framework designed to enhance the accuracy and robustness of fusion processes. The framework addresses the inherent uncertainties and correlations present in multi-modal data by dynamically adjusting fusion weights based on these characteristics. The core mechanism leverages Bayesian networks to probabilistically model each modality and employs information-theoretic measures, specifically entropy and mutual information, to quantify the relationships between modalities. This allows for adaptive weighting schemes, providing a more robust and accurate fusion outcome compared to traditional methods reliant on fixed rules or statistical learning. The framework's novelty lies in its dynamic modeling of modality relationships, offering a flexible approach to complex multi-modal data integration.

title: Quantum State Geometries for Quantum Computing Simulation
abstract: This paper investigates the application of non-linear geometric transformations to quantum states to construct simulation environments for quantum computing. The core claim is that by manipulating the geometric structure of quantum states, we can achieve higher simulation accuracy and efficiency compared to traditional methods. This research explores a novel approach to generating complex geometric representations of quantum states, utilizing these representations to enhance the fidelity of quantum simulations. The paper details a method for creating a non-linear transformation that converts a quantum state into a complex geometric structure, and details how this structure is exploited to facilitate accurate simulations. The study focuses on the potential for this geometric approach to overcome limitations of existing simulation techniques.

title: Cognitive Architectures for Embodied AI with Bayesian Inference
abstract: This paper proposes a novel cognitive architecture for embodied artificial intelligence (AI) systems, designed to address the limitations of current approaches. The architecture leverages principles of cognitive science, specifically Bayesian inference, hierarchical control, and reinforcement learning, to facilitate robust learning and adaptation within complex, dynamic environments. The core claim is that existing embodied AI systems lack a holistic cognitive architecture capable of seamlessly integrating perception, action, and learning. The developed architecture aims to overcome this deficiency by providing a structured framework for representing knowledge, planning actions, and updating beliefs based on sensory input and interaction. Key components include a Bayesian inference engine for probabilistic reasoning, a hierarchical control system for managing complex behaviors, and reinforcement learning algorithms for optimizing actions and achieving goals. This integrated approach promises to significantly enhance the capabilities of embodied AI agents, enabling them to navigate, learn, and interact with the world in a more intelligent and adaptive manner. The architecture is presented as a modular system, allowing for flexibility and extensibility as the field of embodied AI continues to evolve. This document outlines the architectural design, the underlying principles, and the anticipated benefits of this approach.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Storage Protocol
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed storage protocol leveraging quantum entanglement to enhance security and resilience against attacks. Traditional distributed storage systems rely on classical cryptographic algorithms, which are vulnerable to advances in computing power and algorithmic breakthroughs. This protocol aims to mitigate these vulnerabilities by directly exploiting the principles of quantum mechanics, specifically quantum entanglement, for secure data storage and retrieval. The core idea is to establish entangled states between storage nodes. Data encryption and verification are then performed by manipulating these entangled states, eliminating the need for conventional key exchange processes. This approach offers a fundamentally different security paradigm, providing a higher level of confidentiality and resistance against attacks that target classical cryptographic assumptions. The protocol's efficiency and scalability will be explored conceptually, laying the groundwork for future research and potential implementation.

The protocol's efficiency and scalability will be explored conceptually, laying the groundwork for future research and potential implementation.

title: Evolutionary Symbolic Program Generation and Verification
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to program generation and verification by integrating evolutionary algorithms with symbolic execution techniques. The core idea is to leverage the search capabilities of evolutionary algorithms to discover optimal program representations (symbols) and then employ symbolic program generation to translate these symbols into executable code. Crucially, formal verification methods are applied to ensure the correctness of the generated code. The system automates a traditionally manual and often error-prone process, significantly enhancing both efficiency and reliability. We demonstrate the feasibility and potential of this combined approach through a detailed explanation of the methodology and theoretical underpinnings. The resulting system offers a pathway towards automated software development and verification, particularly for complex systems where manual design and exhaustive testing are impractical.

title: Federated Learning with Differential Privacy and Personalized Model Aggregation
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without direct data sharing. However, traditional FL methods are vulnerable to information leakage and model divergence, particularly when dealing with highly heterogeneous client datasets. This research proposes a novel framework that combines differential privacy (DP) with personalized model aggregation (PMA) to mitigate these issues. The core claim is that integrating DP safeguards client data while PMA allows for adaptation of the global model to individual client characteristics. We introduce a rigorous methodology for quantifying the trade-offs between privacy, model accuracy, and computational overhead. The proposed approach enhances both the robustness and effectiveness of FL systems, paving the way for more secure and adaptable distributed learning applications. Specifically, we formulate the aggregation process using the following notation: Let $m_i$ represent the model received from client *i*, $s_i$ be the local data used by client *i*, and $\epsilon$ and $\delta$ be the privacy parameters. The personalized aggregation function is defined as: $m_{aggregated} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{K} \alpha_i * m_i}{\sum_{i=1}^{K} \alpha_i}$ where $\alpha_i$ are weights determined based on client data characteristics and privacy constraints. We leverage differential privacy by adding noise to the model updates, represented as: $m_i' = m_i + \epsilon * N(0, I_d)$ where $N(0, I_d)$ denotes Gaussian noise with mean 0 and covariance matrix $I_d$ (d-dimensional identity matrix).

title: Hierarchical Latent Variable Discovery via Bayesian Deep Belief Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for hierarchical latent variable discovery within complex datasets leveraging Bayesian Deep Belief Networks (BDBNs). The core challenge in latent variable discovery lies in both the dimensionality of the problem and the inherent ambiguity in interpreting the discovered factors. Traditional methods often struggle with scalability and providing meaningful explanations for the identified latent structures. Our approach addresses these limitations by employing a deep belief network architecture with explicitly modeled hierarchical layers, combined with Bayesian inference to quantify uncertainty. This allows us to not only identify groupings of latent variables but also to assess their reliability. The resulting representations are expected to be more interpretable and robust. We propose a framework for training BDBNs with a hierarchical structure, incorporating prior knowledge and utilizing variational inference to estimate the posterior distribution over the latent variables. This approach offers a significant improvement over standard deep learning methods in terms of interpretability and uncertainty quantification, ultimately leading to more actionable insights from complex data. The methodology presented here facilitates the automatic construction of hierarchical latent variable models, promoting a deeper understanding of underlying data patterns.

title: Quantum System Self-Adaptive Noise Parameter Adjustment
abstract: Quantum system noise represents a significant challenge to achieving precise control and optimization in quantum computation. This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive algorithm for quantum system noise parameter adjustment, designed to dynamically adjust noise parameters based on the system's inherent dynamic behavior. The core mechanism leverages a feedback loop that continuously monitors and responds to noise fluctuations, ensuring stability and accuracy throughout the quantum process. This approach offers a significant improvement over static parameter adjustment methods, enabling more robust and adaptable control over quantum systems. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through simulations, showcasing its ability to maintain coherence and achieve targeted quantum operations with reduced sensitivity to noise fluctuations.

title: 基于自适应的变量空间理论
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm, termed "Adaptive Variable Space Theory" (AVST), designed to optimize performance in complex, non-linear systems. Traditional variable space theories often rely on manual parameter tuning, limiting their ability to effectively address data-driven challenges. AVST dynamically adjusts the shape and structure of the variable space based on the characteristics of the input data, offering a more automated and adaptable approach. This paper details the core concepts, mechanism, and initial results of AVST, demonstrating its efficacy in a range of applications. The algorithm's strength lies in its capacity to automatically optimize parameters, leading to improved performance compared to existing methods. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance and discuss future research directions.

title: Quantum State Dynamic Topology Parameter Adjustment
abstract: Quantum state dynamic topology parameter adjustment is a novel approach to optimizing quantum systems, particularly for complex calculations. This paper introduces a new algorithm based on analyzing quantum state dynamics and dynamically adjusting topology to enhance quantum system performance. We detail the core mechanism, leveraging the unique properties of quantum states to automatically tailor the quantum system's topology, leading to improved computational efficiency. The algorithm's efficacy is demonstrated through a comprehensive analysis of a specific quantum system, showcasing its potential for significantly enhancing quantum computations.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm, the Dynamic-Graph Quantum Algorithm, designed to enhance the efficiency of quantum computations by leveraging the unique properties of dynamic graphs. The Dynamic-Graph Quantum Algorithm utilizes dynamic graph structures to guide the optimization process, offering a fundamentally new approach to quantum circuit design and execution. This work explores the potential of dynamic graph structure in quantum computing and proposes a method for improving the performance and scalability of quantum algorithms.

title: 基于自适应的神经网络的动态正则化策略
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic regularization strategy based on adaptive neural networks. Traditional regularization techniques often rely on fixed parameters and static training data, limiting their ability to adapt to changing input data. This work proposes a framework that dynamically adjusts the regularization strength based on the input data's dynamics, enhancing both network performance and stability. The core mechanism involves a self-adaptive neural network that learns and adjusts the regularization coefficients in real-time. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experiments on various benchmark datasets, showcasing improved accuracy, robustness, and generalization capabilities compared to existing regularization methods.

title: 基于自适应学习的量子计算的拓扑密度优化
abstract: Quantum computing offers the potential for unprecedented computational power, but realizing this potential requires careful management of quantum states. The stability and efficiency of quantum computations are highly dependent on the precise control and optimization of these states. This paper investigates a novel quantum computing optimization algorithm based on adaptive learning, specifically designed to dynamically adjust quantum potential fields to enhance stability and efficiency. We propose a mechanism that iteratively adjusts the quantum potential, responding to changes in the system, to achieve optimal quantum states. The core claim of this work is that the proposed adaptive learning approach can significantly improve the performance of quantum computations compared to traditional optimization methods. This is achieved through a dynamic and responsive quantum potential landscape, allowing for more efficient exploration of the state space. The paper details the algorithm's implementation, demonstrates its effectiveness through simulations, and discusses the potential implications for future quantum computing development.

title: Quantum Simulation of Complex Fluid Dynamics with Adaptive Resolution
abstract: Quantum Simulation of Complex Fluid Dynamics with Adaptive Resolution Abstract: This paper proposes a novel quantum simulation framework for turbulent flow dynamics, incorporating a self-tuning resolution strategy. Current simulation methods often rely on fixed resolution, limiting accuracy, particularly in regions of high complexity. We demonstrate that our approach, utilizing quantum entanglement and superposition, dynamically adjusts the simulation's resolution based on input data, resulting in significantly improved accuracy and reduced computational cost for turbulent flows. The core mechanism involves manipulating the quantum state of a simplified fluid element to effectively represent the complex flow pattern, offering a scalable and efficient alternative to traditional methods. The potential impact of this work is a shift towards more accurate and computationally feasible turbulence modeling.

title: Quantum Topologies for Adaptive Quantum Computing
abstract: Quantum Topologies offer a novel approach to quantum computation, leveraging the intricate properties of quantum geometry to create highly resilient and adaptable quantum systems. This paper investigates a framework for adaptive quantum computation based on quantum topology, focusing on the design of an algorithm that dynamically adjusts quantum state parameters based on input data. We propose a method for generating and manipulating quantum states using topological properties, demonstrating its potential to overcome limitations of conventional quantum computing. The core mechanism centers around the application of topological invariants to guide quantum state evolution, leading to enhanced computational performance. This work presents a conceptual design and preliminary results exploring the feasibility of this approach, highlighting the advantages of quantum topology in achieving more efficient and robust quantum computation.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Operational Intelligence: A Technical Architecture for AI-Powered Field Service Automation
abstract: This paper presents a technical architecture for AI-powered operational intelligence in field service management, as implemented in FieldMind AI (GFM). The architecture combines workflow orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounded in a vector-indexed operational knowledge base, and a multi-channel communication gateway into a unified system capable of interpreting operational signals — chemical readings, equipment alerts, inventory levels — and generating context-aware, prioritized responses. We describe each architectural layer, the design rationale behind key technical choices, and trade-offs relevant to deploying this class of system for small and independent field service businesses.

title: Deep Learning in Multimodal Breast Cancer Imaging: From Image Reconstruction and Segmentation to Diagnosis and Treatment Response Prediction
abstract: Breast cancer imaging is central to screening, diagnosis, staging, treatment monitoring, and post-treatment surveillance, but image interpretation remains limited by variable image quality, interobserver variability, false-positive findings and heterogeneous tumor biology. This narrative review summarizes current applications of deep learning in multimodal breast cancer imaging, with emphasis on image reconstruction, image enhancement, lesion detection, segmentation, classification, biomarker prediction, treatment response assessment, prognosis and clinical implementation. A structured literature search was performed across major biomedical and technical databases, focusing on studies involving mammography, digital breast tomosynthesis, ultrasound, MRI, PET/CT, digital pathology and multimodal fusion approaches. Current evidence indicates that deep learning can support image denoising; super-resolution, low-dose, and accelerated reconstruction; lesion localization; tumor segmentation; benign–malignant classification; and molecular or biomarker-related prediction. Multimodal models integrating radiological imaging, histopathology, clinical variables, and molecular markers show particular promise for treatment response prediction, recurrence risk estimation, and personalized decision support. However, clinical translation remains limited by retrospective study designs, small and imbalanced datasets, domain shift, inconsistent annotations, limited explainability, bias, lack of prospective validation, and regulatory challenges. Deep learning should therefore be viewed as a decision-support framework that may improve breast cancer imaging workflows if validated in diverse, prospective, and clinically representative settings.

title: A Resource-Efficient End-to-End Multimodal AI Framework for Automated PET-CT Report Generation and TNM Staging in Breast Cancer
abstract: Objectives: Positron Emission Tomography-Computed Tomography (PET-CT) is integral to breast cancer staging. However, manual interpretation is time-consuming and subject to inter-observer variability. While artificial intelligence has shown promise in lesion detection and standardised uptake value (SUVmax) quantification, existing approaches are fragmented and do not generate complete TNM-aligned structured reports. Consequently, there remains a need for an integrated framework capable of translating PET-CT data into structured clinical reports. Material and Methods: We developed a Multimodal Report Generator (MMRG) as an exploratory pilot study using data from 85 breast cancer patients (439 clusters; 59/15/11 train/validation/test). The framework combines tri-planar Swin3D feature extraction, multimodal feature fusion, multi-task lesion analysis, and (Generative Pre-trained Transformer) GPT-2-based report generation with Facebook AI Similarity Search (FAISS) retrieval-augmented generation. The entire pipeline was trained on a single consumer-grade graphics processing unit (GPU), supporting a resource-efficient design. Results: Model Training demonstrated stable convergence without evidence of train-validation divergence. At the selected validation checkpoint (15 patients, 50 clusters), lesion detection achieved a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.861 and an F1 score of 0.757, while descriptor classification achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.787 and an F1 score of 0.757. SUVmax and lesion-size estimation showed Pearson correlations of 0.44 and 0.64, respectively. On the held-out internal test set ( n = 11 patients, 61 clusters), lesion detection achieved an ROC-AUC of 0.857, an F1 score of 0.652, and a Cohen’s κ of 0.466, while descriptor classification achieved an ROC-AUC of 0.759, an F1 score of 0.546, and a κ of 0.381. Quantitative estimation yielded SUVmax mean absolute error (MAE) = 6.44 (Pearson r = 0.49) and lesion-size MAE = 0.73 cm (Pearson r = 0.34). Tumour-Node-Metastasis (TNM) staging accuracy was 18.2%, with M-stage accuracy of 63.6%. The organ-domain hallucination rate was 35.7% on breast-cancer-relevant test clusters. The framework successfully generated structured PET-CT reports with automated lesion description and TNM staging. Conclusion: This exploratory pilot study demonstrates the feasibility of an end-to-end multimodal AI pipeline for PET-CT interpretation in breast cancer, combining lesion detection, quantitative measurement, structured report generation, and TNM staging within a single framework. While lesion- and descriptor-classification showed encouraging performance, TNM staging results remain preliminary in this small cohort. The framework is presented as a resource-efficient prototype for future larger-cohort studies rather than a clinically validated deployment-ready system. Future work will focus on larger multi-centre datasets, improved quantitative estimation, and direct or joint TNM-stage prediction architectures.
