title: Автоматизированная контент генерация в SMM на B2B рынке информационных технологий
abstract: Целью работы является создание, обучение и оценка эффективности специализированного программного инструмента для автоматизированной генерации B2B-контента на базе больших языковых моделей (LLM). Методология проведения работы включает теоретический анализ предметной области, методы сбора и предварительной обработки естественного языка, семантический обратный инжиниринг, а также методы эффективного дообучения нейронных сетей (QLoRA, SFT, IPO) и автоматизированной оценки качества текстов с использованием парадигмы LLM-as-a-Judge. В ходе работы получены следующие основные результаты: сформирован репрезентативный датасет из 40 000 публикаций ИТ-компаний в Telegram; произведено дообучение языковой модели Gemma-4; реализован полноценный вычислительный конвейер генерации контента. Сравнительный анализ показал, что модель, прошедшая этап SFT, демонстрирует наивысшую эффективность при создании глубоких технических гайдов, тогда как базовая модель лучше справляется с форматом классических кейс-стади. Областью применения результатов работы являются маркетинговые отделы и SMM-агентства, специализирующиеся на продвижении продуктов и услуг в корпоративном секторе (B2B ИТ). Внедрение разработанного инструмента на базе LLM решает проблему «бутылочного горлышка» технической экспертизы в ИТ-маркетинге. Использование дообученной модели позволяет делегировать искусственному интеллекту перевод сложной инженерной информации на язык профессионального маркетинга, что снижает удельные затраты на производство контента и повышает рентабельность маркетинговых инвестиций без потери фактологической точности.

В ходе работы получены следующие основные результаты: сформирован репрезентативный датасет из 40 000 публикаций ИТ-компаний в Telegram; произведено дообучение языковой модели Gemma-4; реализован полноценный вычислительный конвейер генерации контента. Сравнительный анализ показал, что модель, прошедшая этап SFT, демонстрирует наивысшую эффективность при создании глубоких технических гайдов, тогда как базовая модель лучше справляется с форматом классических кейс-стади. Областью применения результатов работы являются маркетинговые отделы и SMM-агентства, специализирующиеся на продвижении продуктов и услуг в корпоративном секторе (B2B ИТ). Внедрение разработанного инструмента на базе LLM решает проблему «бутылочного горлышка» технической экспертизы в ИТ-маркетинге. Использование дообученной модели позволяет делегировать искусственному интеллекту перевод сложной инженерной информации на язык профессионального маркетинга, что снижает удельные затраты на производство контента и повышает рентабельность маркетинговых инвестиций без потери фактологической точности.

title: CROCODIL: Cross-Model Code Editing with LLMs
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have become ubiquitous tools for code generation and editing. However, development teams often use multiple LLM assistants. Different developers may prefer different models, and individual developers may switch between models across different coding sessions. Because of this, the edits any one model makes are frequently applied to foreign code originally generated by another model. These LLMs are often trained on different datasets, and as a result have different stylistic preferences. Do LLMs behave differently when they edit foreign code originally written by a different LLM with a different coding style? We find that models tend to make more, and often excessive, edits on foreign code. We introduce CROCODIL (Cross-model Code Editing with LLMs), a post-training framework for reducing excessive edits while preserving functional correctness. CROCODIL's similarity reward penalizes large changes, while its execution reward scores build and test success. We use the product of these two rewards to encourage the policy to decrease the edit size without decreasing the edit task success rate. CROCODIL is available at https://github.com/EngineeringSoftware/Crocodil.

title: Coupled Scaling: A Representational Accessibility Framework for Neural Scaling Laws
abstract: We ask when two learning systems trained on the same task under a common resource protocol should share a scaling rate and when their rates should differ. Coupled Scaling answers this through representational accessibility: the task-relevant geometry that a specified architecture-optimization system can reach and how that geometry is acquired as resources grow. In an orthogonal model, unsupported target energy sets the asymptotic floor, while unacquired supported energy sets the finite-budget residual. When acquisition can skip high-value directions, the largest fully acquired prefix no longer determines a unique exponent. For target powers $a_j \asymp j^{-b}$, $b>1$, and prefix log-growth rate $0<ρ\leq1$, the sharp attainable interval is $[ρ(b-1),\min\{b-1,ρb\}]$, and every rate in this interval is realized by a fixed acquisition order on a common support. A rank-window condition identifies when the product law $α=ρ(b-1)$ applies, while a fixed-kernel specialization expresses the same task-system dependence through the task-weighted spectral tail. We then audit released capability trajectories to diagnose measurement and comparison effects and propose a staged test in which independently measured geometry predicts held-out loss, scaling rates, and cross-task reversals.

title: Efficient Constant Optimization for Symbolic Regression with GPU-Accelerated Tree-Based Genetic Programming
abstract: Constant optimization refines the numerical coefficients of candidate expressions in tree-based genetic programming for symbolic regression. But its per-generation cost has led modern GPU-accelerated frameworks to omit it or restrict it to lightweight forms. We present a GPU-resident, batched Levenberg--Marquardt solver that optimizes constants across a structurally heterogeneous population of expression trees using a fixed number of population-wide CUDA launches per iteration. Reverse-mode automatic differentiation assembles the per-tree Jacobian in one backward sweep, making the dominant per-iteration cost independent of the number of constants per tree, and a double-precision delivery guard guarantees that returned constants are never worse than their initial values. On early-generation populations, the solver sustains up to $5.1{\times}10^{5}$ trees per second on an NVIDIA A100; at a GPU-saturated benchmark configuration it delivers roughly $9.9{\times}$ the throughput of Operon running on a 64-core EPYC 7763, while matching fp64-reference quality. Integrated in-process into EvoGP, the solver enables end-to-end search to recover governing equations on $10$ of $18$ constructed problems versus 0 for stock EvoGP. Our code is at https://github.com/TensorConv/CuSR.

title: Bayesian Spectral Decomposition for Differential Geometry
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Bayesian Spectral Decomposition (BSD) algorithm for geometric object representation and evolution. Traditional methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the flexibility and adaptability of geometric models. BSD leverages a probabilistic framework, updating posterior distributions of geometric object parameters as new data is observed. The algorithm efficiently captures complex geometric shapes and allows for accurate prediction of their evolution. We present a detailed theoretical analysis and practical implementation of the algorithm, demonstrating its effectiveness through simulations and a simplified case study. This approach offers a robust and adaptable representation for geometric modeling, reducing the need for extensive parameter tuning. The core mechanism lies in iteratively refining the posterior distribution of geometric object parameters using Bayesian inference, enabling the algorithm to handle complex geometries and provide accurate predictions.

title: Title: Hierarchical Bayesian Model for Dynamical Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel hierarchical Bayesian model designed to address the challenges inherent in modeling dynamical systems. Traditional approaches often struggle with accurately capturing long-term dependencies and the intricate relationships between variables at different levels of granularity. Our model leverages Bayesian inference to dynamically update state probabilities, creating a nested hierarchy that facilitates more precise prediction and enhanced understanding of system behavior. We introduce a framework for representing states as a hierarchical structure, enabling the modeling of dependencies across multiple scales. The core mechanism involves iteratively refining state probabilities based on observed data, fostering a more robust and adaptable representation of the system. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations exploring various dynamical systems, highlighting its ability to improve long-term forecasting accuracy compared to existing methods.

title: 基于自适应的分布式量子计算算法优化框架
abstract: Distributed quantum computing (DQC) offers immense potential for tackling complex computational problems, but its realization faces significant challenges related to algorithm design, parameter optimization, and scalability. This paper proposes a novel algorithm optimization framework for DQC, centered around a dynamically adaptive quantum state self-adaptation mechanism. The framework leverages the inherent complexity of DQC to automatically adjust quantum parameters, ultimately enhancing the precision and efficiency of computations while enabling support for large-scale quantum systems. We introduce a mechanism to continuously monitor and adjust parameters based on the quantum state, leading to improved performance characteristics. This work addresses the limitations of existing optimization techniques and paves the way for more robust and efficient DQC systems. The core mechanism focuses on a self-tuning approach, dynamically adjusting the quantum state based on the current computation, thereby optimizing performance. This research presents a framework that can dynamically adjust parameters, improving the overall quality of computations.

title: Nonlinear Topological Structures in Adaptive Quantum Information Coding
abstract: Quantum information is a fundamental resource in modern technology, demanding robust security measures. Traditional quantum information encoding methods often fall short in this regard, particularly when security is paramount. This paper investigates the application of non-linear topological structures to adaptive quantum information encoding, exploring a novel approach that leverages dynamic adjustments to the topology to enhance both the fidelity and security of quantum information transmission. We propose a mechanism that utilizes a self-adaptive topology to dynamically adjust the encoding parameters, ensuring optimal performance against potential attacks. The core claim is that this design significantly improves quantum information security through enhanced robustness and adaptability.

title: Autonomous Theorem Proving with Neural Network-Guided Search
abstract: This paper explores the potential of integrating neural networks into the process of autonomous theorem proving to significantly improve efficiency. Traditional autonomous theorem provers often struggle with combinatorial explosion, leading to prolonged proof search times. This work proposes a novel approach where a neural network is trained to predict the most promising proof strategies given the current state of the proof process. The network's predictive capabilities aim to guide the theorem prover's search, focusing computational resources on potentially fruitful avenues. We outline the core components of this system, detailing the neural network architecture, training methodology, and integration strategy with a standard theorem proving framework. The key contribution lies in the ability of a machine learning model to learn and adapt to the specific nuances of a given proof task, offering a dynamic and potentially far more efficient approach to automated reasoning compared to traditional, rule-based search algorithms. The presented framework represents a step toward creating truly intelligent theorem provers capable of tackling complex mathematical problems with increased speed and reliability.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Reinforcement Learning with Latent State Representations
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of probabilistic programming languages (PPLs) in conjunction with latent state representations for reinforcement learning (RL). Traditional RL methods often struggle with exploration, generalization, and robustness, particularly in complex and partially observable environments. We propose a novel framework where the environment's state is modeled as a distribution over latent states, and a PPL is employed to define the agent's policy and value function. This approach enables Bayesian inference, allowing the agent to quantify uncertainty and improve exploration strategies. Furthermore, leveraging latent representations facilitates generalization by capturing underlying structure within the state space. The core claim of this work is that this combined approach significantly enhances exploration, generalization, and robustness in RL. We outline the key components of this framework and discuss the benefits of incorporating PPLs for improved learning performance, emphasizing the ability to reason about uncertainty and adapt to novel situations. The methodology presented offers a promising direction for developing more sophisticated and reliable RL agents.

title: Self-Organizing Topological Quantum Computing Simulation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum computing simulation leveraging the principles of self-organization in topological quantum matter. We develop a simulation tool, termed "Topological Echo Simulation" (TES), designed to emulate complex quantum phenomena, including topological order, spin configuration, and entanglement, by mimicking the self-organizing behavior of topological phases. The TES utilizes a modified quantum state representation to accurately represent and simulate the evolution of these topological structures. The core mechanism involves generating and manipulating a highly complex, dynamically evolving quantum state, guided by a carefully designed topological algorithm, which produces a topologically robust and coherent simulation. The paper details the TES's architecture, the underlying mathematical framework, and the simulation process, highlighting its potential for advanced quantum simulation and its contribution to the exploration of quantum topological physics. The focus is on demonstrating the tool's capabilities through illustrative examples and preliminary results focusing on the simulation of a simple topological phase, demonstrating the feasibility of the proposed method.

title: Non-Euclidean Constraint Optimization with Dynamic Topology (NCO-DT)
abstract: This paper introduces Non-Euclidean Constraint Optimization with Dynamic Topology (NCO-DT), a novel approach to complex optimization problems. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with high-dimensional spaces and intricate structural dependencies, leading to suboptimal solutions. NCO-DT addresses this challenge by employing a dynamically adaptive topology, allowing the system to reformulate itself based on real-time assessment of the problem's characteristics. This adaptation facilitates the exploration of a broader solution space and enhances the robustness of the optimization process. The core mechanism centers around a 'Adaptive Topology Mapping' algorithm, which iteratively refines the system's geometry while maintaining the objective function's constraints. We demonstrate the effectiveness of NCO-DT through a series of case studies involving diverse optimization challenges, showcasing its ability to surpass conventional methods in terms of solution quality and computational efficiency.

abstract: The pursuit of efficient computation necessitates the exploration of novel algorithmic paradigms. This paper introduces a novel computational framework, "Quantum Topological Self-Adaptive Computing" (QTASC), leveraging the principles of quantum topology to enhance the process of structure discovery and optimization. We propose a method for automatically identifying and optimizing computational pathways based on the inherent topology of the problem space. QTASC's core mechanism hinges on the ability to exploit quantum entanglement and superposition to reveal underlying structural patterns that are crucial for efficient computation. This approach promises to significantly improve computational efficiency, particularly for complex problems involving intricate data structures. The paper details the theoretical foundation of QTASC, presents a preliminary implementation illustrating its efficacy, and discusses future research directions aimed at expanding the framework's capabilities.

title: Adaptive Network Self-Adaptive Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative self-organizing network framework designed to enhance predictive accuracy through dynamic parameter adjustment. Traditional optimization methods often lack the flexibility to respond effectively to evolving system states, leading to suboptimal performance. Our proposed algorithm leverages a self-organizing network architecture, dynamically adjusting model parameters based on real-time feedback. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously monitors the system's state and adjusts parameters to minimize prediction error. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and preliminary experiments, showcasing significant improvements in prediction accuracy compared to conventional optimization techniques.

title: Self-Organizing Neural Networks for Robot Navigation in Dynamic Environments
abstract: This paper investigates the application of self-organizing neural networks (SOMs) to robot navigation within dynamic environments. Traditional robot navigation often relies on explicit programming or reinforcement learning, which can be challenging to implement and adapt to unforeseen changes. This work proposes a novel approach utilizing SOMs to enable robots to autonomously learn and execute navigation strategies. The core idea is to map the environment into a self-organized structure, where neurons representing different regions adapt to the robot's surroundings through proximity and interaction. This eliminates the need for predefined rules and allows the robot to dynamically adjust its behavior in response to changing conditions. The paper details the SOM architecture, the learning process, and the resulting navigation capabilities. We demonstrate the potential of this approach to achieve robust and adaptive navigation in complex, dynamic scenarios.

title: Title: Geometric Formalism for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel geometric formalism for multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) systems, aiming to enhance the stability and interpretability of algorithms. Traditional MARL approaches often struggle with complex interactions and the difficulty in understanding the decision-making processes within these systems. We propose a framework that represents agent interactions as geometric graphs, explicitly modeling proximity, connectivity, and preferential paths. This geometric representation allows for a more intuitive and structured analysis of the system's dynamics, facilitating the identification of critical decision points and potential convergence issues. The paper details the implementation of this geometric formalism, explores its impact on algorithm performance, and discusses potential future directions for research. The core claim is that this geometric approach significantly improves the robustness and interpretability of MARL systems, offering a shift towards a more formalized and comprehensible approach to complex decision-making.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to probabilistic modeling, termed the Domain-Adaptive Probability Model (DAPM), designed to dynamically adjust model parameters based on the characteristics of the input domain. The core innovation lies in employing a dynamically evolving probability model that adapts to the specific nuances of the data, leading to improved predictive accuracy compared to static parameter tuning methods. The system's effectiveness is demonstrated through a series of rigorous experiments across multiple datasets. The proposed method offers a significant step towards automated and optimized probabilistic modeling, particularly in scenarios involving diverse and complex data sets.

title: Quantum State Vector Reconstruction via Bayesian Inference
abstract: Quantum state vector reconstruction is a fundamental problem in quantum information theory, crucial for tasks like quantum state tomography and quantum error correction. Traditional methods often struggle with noisy measurements and lack a principled framework for uncertainty quantification. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, Quantum State Vector Reconstruction via Bayesian Inference, that leverages Bayesian inference to reconstruct a quantum state vector from a set of measurements, enhancing accuracy and offering a more robust approach compared to existing methods. We detail the core mechanism, emphasizing the integration of Bayesian estimation for uncertainty quantification and refinement of the reconstruction process. The algorithm incorporates a probabilistic approach to estimate the state vector distribution, improving reconstruction by incorporating uncertainty estimates directly into the reconstruction process. This results in a more reliable and accurate state vector reconstruction, particularly when dealing with noisy measurements. This work addresses the limitations of conventional methods by providing a principled Bayesian framework for state vector reconstruction, offering a significant advancement in this field.

title: Quantum Entropy Dynamics Model and Optimization
abstract: Quantum entropy dynamics models offer a novel approach to optimizing quantum computation and information processing. This paper explores the construction of a quantum entropy dynamics model, leveraging the unique properties of quantum entropy to design optimization algorithms specifically tailored for quantum systems. The core claim is that establishing this model will enhance quantum computation's performance and efficiency through the application of quantum entropy principles. This work investigates the integration of quantum entropy with quantum dynamics, utilizing the inherent characteristics of quantum entropy to guide the optimization of quantum systems. The resultant optimization algorithms demonstrate potential for substantial performance gains in various quantum computing tasks.

title: Title: Non-Linear Topological Maps for Data Compression
abstract: This paper explores the application of novel non-linear topological maps for data compression. Traditional compression techniques often rely on discrete data representations and can struggle with complex data. We propose a new class of topological maps, designed to dynamically adapt to the data's structure, offering superior compression ratios compared to existing methods. The core mechanism centers around a self-replicating topology that intelligently expands and contracts to represent the data, leveraging a sparse encoding scheme. This approach aims to create a 'compressed' representation that minimizes redundancy while maintaining data integrity. We detail the mathematical framework of this approach, including the defining topological space, the self-replicating element, and the encoding process. The paper concludes with a discussion of the experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this new method, highlighting its potential for significant improvements in data compression.

title: Quantum Adaptive Time Series Prediction
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Quantum Adaptive Time Series Prediction (QATSP) algorithm, designed to enhance prediction accuracy by dynamically adjusting model parameters based on historical data. Traditional forecasting methods rely heavily on human design, while QATSP leverages quantum self-adaptational principles to achieve superior performance through continuous optimization. The core mechanism involves a quantum-enhanced temporal evolution of a prediction model, allowing for real-time adjustments informed by observed data patterns. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a series of simulations and experimental analysis, showcasing significant improvements in prediction fidelity compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions, including exploring the scalability of the quantum adaptation process and its potential application to diverse time series datasets.

title: Training Without Gathering the Data: A Interdisciplinary Mapping Review of Federated Learning and Privacy-Preserving AI
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Federated Learning and Privacy-Preserving AI in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of federated learning and privacy as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Betwixt
abstract: Semantic knowledge is commonly represented in structures designed for persistence, exchange, or machine reasoning, while human review and much data-processing software operate more naturally on rectangular data. This paper introduces Betwixt, an R implementation of reviewable relational projections for semantic assertions. Betwixt treats atomic subject–predicate–value assertions as independently identifiable semantic units and projects them into tidy long or wider relational forms appropriate to particular review operations. Dual projections additionally align an assertion with another assertion establishing its relationship to evidentiary material, without combining the two into a compound semantic assertion. The resulting representations provide an intermediate layer between semantic models and human-centred review interfaces. The paper distinguishes projection from review semantics, describes the principal projection classes supported by the Betwixt model, and demonstrates their use in constructing reproducible review workspaces while preserving the identities required for subsequent provenance-aware semantic processing.

title: Использование AI – технологий в индустрии туризма и гостеприимства для продвижения туристской дестинации на внутреннем рынке (на примере Республики Карелия)
abstract: Данная работа посвящена разработке AI-ассистента для продвижения туристкой дестинации Республики Карелия. В процессе исследования были решены следующие задачи: 1. Изучение мировых и отечественных практик применения искусственного интеллекта для продвижения туристкой дестинации 2. Исследование рынка туристических услуг Республики Карелия 3. Выявление основных проблем развития и организации туристкой индустрии в рамках объекта исследования 4. Разработка AI-ассистента на основе отечественной LLM 5. Разработка комплекса мер в сфере AI для решения проблем продвижения Республики Карелия как туристкой дестинации на внутреннем рынке туризма В ходе работы были рассмотрены основные практики применения искусственного интеллекта в сфере туризма, их преимущества и недостатки. Были выявлены основные проблемы Республики Карелия в сфере развития и организации туристкой индустрии. Результатом работы стала разработка для Республики Карелия комплекса мер в сфере AI для решения проблем продвижения Республики как туристкой дестинации на внутреннем рынке туризма, а также разработка AI-ассистента на основе данных решений. Для достижения данных результатов в работе были использованы/разработаны следующие информационные технологии, в том числе программное обеспечение, облачные сервисы, базы данных и прочие: текстовый, графический редактор и электронные таблицы.

title: XAI Decoded
abstract: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) aims to close that gap by producing human-understandable outputs that establish trust, transparency, and accountability between people and AI systems. This chapter provides a systematic literature review (SLR), according to PRISMA, to analyze peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2024. The review also differentiates between local and global explanation methods in terms of whether they concentrate on individual predictions or on general model behavior. Based on our findings, SHAP and LIME are overwhelmingly used in practice because they work with black-box models and are easy to implement, although the two methods differ in their theoretical foundation and computational complexity. Despite the increasing relevance of XAI in safety-critical areas such as healthcare, finance, and autonomous systems, open issues remain concerning the sacrifice of interpretability in favor of accuracy, the absence of standardized evaluation metrics, and human-focused design.

title: Introduction
abstract: This chapter provides a comprehensive foundation for the entire book by introducing the core concepts, scope, and significance of sentiment analysis in natural language processing. It begins with an overview of sentiment analysis as a key subfield that extracts subjective information from textual, audio, and visual data. The chapter systematically defines sentiment analysis, explores its three primary modalities (textual, audio, and visual), and outlines its expanded scope, including multimodal analysis, industry-specific applications, real-time processing, cross-cultural challenges, and ethical concerns. It further discusses the growing importance of sentiment analysis in business intelligence, public safety, public health, finance, politics, and e-commerce, supported by a detailed table of applications across domains. The historical evolution, research significance, current challenges, and future directions are also examined. Finally, the chapter presents the overall structure of the book, describing how each subsequent chapter builds upon the previous ones to guide readers from foundational concepts to advanced techniques and practical applications.

title: Well-posedness of Filtering Equations in Weighted Sobolev Spaces with Unbounded System Coefficients
abstract: Nonlinear filtering problem is one of the core subjects in modern control theory. In this paper, we will study the well-posedness of the three fundamental evolution equations arising in continuous-time nonlinear filtering--the robust Duncan-Mortensen-Zakai (DMZ) equation, the stochastic DMZ equation, and the Kushner-Stratonovich equation--within a unified buffered weighted formulation. An exponential-type weight function and the corresponding weighted Sobolev spaces are introduced to enable a variational treatment of the filtering equations in a more general setting, in which the coefficients of the filtering system may be unbounded with polynomial growth. Under mild and easily verifiable assumptions, we first establish the well-posedness of the weak solution to the robust DMZ equation in these weighted spaces. Using the gauge (exponential) transformation and its inverse, these results are then transferred to the stochastic DMZ equation and the Kushner-Stratonovich equation, whose solutions are shown to exist and be unique in buffered weighted Sobolev spaces, yielding a unified treatment of all three filtering equations. Sufficient conditions for the well-posedness are also summarized, which illustrate the wide applicability of the proposed framework to general nonlinear filtering systems.

title: A Prompt-Engineering Approach to Develop Scalable, Flexible, and Real-Time Hybrid Micro-Level Personalization in a General Purpose AI Teaching Assistant
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) teaching assistants powered by large language models (LLMs) offer scalable educational support but often provide limited personalization. This study presents a prompt-engineering-based framework for personalizing general-purpose LLM/RAG-based AI teaching assistants such as Jill Watson across academic disciplines and courses. The framework adapts responses using six learner-specific dimensions: self-assessment, abstraction preference, verbosity preference, perceptual orientation, information processing style, and level of understanding, yielding 96 distinct learner profiles. Student queries are additionally analyzed using Bloom's Taxonomy to estimate cognitive complexity at the interaction level. Learner attributes and cognitive assessments are encoded in structured prompts that condition the LLM without requiring model retraining. The framework is evaluated through experiments using NLP metrics and a human study with five participants. Results show perceived differences in response style and structure across personalization conditions, with statistical analyses identifying learner attributes associated with measurable response changes. These findings provide preliminary evidence that prompt-based personalization can support adaptive behavior in LLM-powered educational agents.

title: Adaptive Quantum Loop
abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational framework, the Adaptive Quantum Loop, designed to precisely model quantum system evolution through dynamic parameter adjustment. Traditional approaches often rely on empirical tuning, while our framework leverages a robust parameter adjustment mechanism to significantly enhance both computational accuracy and efficiency. The core mechanism centers around intelligently adjusting quantum loop parameters to guide the simulation process, resulting in improved fidelity and reduced computational cost. The research explores the potential of this approach in various quantum simulation scenarios and highlights its advantages over existing methods. The paper details the framework's design, mathematical foundations, and experimental validation, demonstrating its effectiveness in modeling complex quantum phenomena.

title: Dynamic Geometry Adjustment Adaptive Model
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic geometry complexity adjustment model for model parameter optimization. Traditional model parameter optimization methods often rely on manual tuning or fixed parameter sets, which can be inefficient and may not always achieve optimal performance. This work proposes a dynamically adjusted model parameter optimization strategy that adapts to the input data's geometric complexity, automatically refining the model's parameters to achieve superior performance. The model utilizes a geometric complexity assessment to intelligently adjust parameters, leading to a more robust and adaptable optimization process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations and experiments, showcasing its ability to efficiently and effectively optimize model performance across a range of scenarios.

title: Title: Quantum Simulation of Complex Dynamical Systems with Hybrid Quantum-Classical Algorithms
abstract: Quantum simulation offers a revolutionary approach to understanding complex dynamical systems, enabling insights into emergent phenomena previously inaccessible through classical methods. This paper explores a novel hybrid quantum-classical algorithm designed to efficiently simulate these systems, combining the strengths of both paradigms. We propose a method for intelligently distributing computational tasks between quantum and classical components, optimizing resource utilization and accelerating the simulation process. The core claim is that this approach can overcome limitations in current quantum simulation techniques, facilitating the study of systems exhibiting complex dynamics and emergent behavior. title: Title: Quantum Entanglement Synchronization via Dynamic Phase Shift
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, offers the potential for instantaneous communication and computation. Traditional approaches to entanglement rely on carefully controlled phase shifts, which, while effective, inherently introduce limitations on speed and responsiveness. This paper explores a novel paradigm for quantum entanglement synchronization – a dynamic phase shift mechanism driven by a complex feedback loop, fundamentally altering the process from a fixed shift to a continuously evolving one. We hypothesize that this approach, leveraging Bayesian statistical analysis, can achieve near-instantaneous synchronization and enable a new generation of quantum computing capabilities. This work presents a theoretical framework and preliminary implementation demonstrating the feasibility of this dynamically adjusted phase shift approach, suggesting a significant departure from current entanglement protocols.

title: Contextualized Memory Networks with Dynamic Knowledge Graph Construction
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to memory network design, termed Contextualized Memory Networks with Dynamic Knowledge Graph Construction (CMN-DKGC). Traditional memory networks often struggle with maintaining relevant information and adapting to varying contexts, leading to performance degradation in complex tasks. Our method addresses this limitation by incorporating a dynamically constructed and updated knowledge graph (KG) that directly reflects the current task context. The KG is continuously learned and refined through interaction with the memory network, enabling the model to prioritize and integrate relevant knowledge. We formalize this process using a series of equations and notations, outlining the core mechanisms and the dynamic update rules for the KG. The key innovation lies in the adaptive nature of the KG, which allows for a more nuanced and context-aware representation of information within the memory network. Experimental results (simulated) demonstrate the effectiveness of CMN-DKGC in improving memory network performance across diverse scenarios. The proposed framework offers a promising direction for building more robust and intelligent memory networks.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for adaptive topology transformations, designed to dynamically adjust the structural characteristics of complex systems and enhance model performance. The core of this approach lies in employing an adaptive algorithm that automatically modifies the topology of a system, allowing for precise control and optimization. We propose a framework built around a self-tuning process, where the algorithm iteratively refines the topology based on a predefined set of criteria and constraints. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this method through several illustrative examples, showcasing its ability to achieve significant improvements in model accuracy and stability compared to traditional approaches. This work presents a practical solution for complex system modeling, offering a pathway to more robust and adaptable models.

title: Random Matrix Logic Dimension Analysis
abstract: This paper investigates the concept of "logic dimension" of random matrices, exploring its potential as a novel computational paradigm for building interpretable machine learning models. The core claim is that analyzing the logical dimension of random matrices can provide valuable insights into the decision-making processes of machine learning models, allowing for a more transparent and understandable approach to model construction. We propose a mechanism where the logical dimension is linked to the model's output, offering a new perspective on model interpretation and potentially uncovering latent relationships within the data. This research aims to establish this connection and demonstrate the practical utility of this approach.

title: Adaptive Meta-Evolutionary Algorithm for Rapid Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel Adaptive Meta-Evolutionary Algorithm (AMEA) designed to address the challenges of rapid adaptation in complex optimization problems. AMEA leverages the principles of meta-learning to create an evolutionary algorithm that can autonomously learn and adapt its parameters and strategies. The core idea is to utilize a meta-learner to guide the evolutionary process, enabling the algorithm to quickly adjust its behavior in response to changes in the objective function or problem constraints. Experimental results, although not presented through dedicated experimentation, demonstrate the potential of AMEA to achieve superior performance compared to traditional evolutionary algorithms, particularly in scenarios requiring rapid adaptation and generalization. The algorithm's adaptive nature allows it to effectively navigate diverse optimization landscapes, leading to improved convergence rates and solution quality. This work contributes to the growing field of meta-learning and its application to evolutionary computation, offering a promising approach for tackling dynamic and uncertain optimization tasks.

abstract: This paper investigates the transformative potential of membrane quantum information theory, proposing a novel approach to quantum information storage and transmission leveraging the inherent self-organization properties of membranes. Furthermore, we delve into the potential applications of this architecture, extending beyond simple qubit storage to encompass complex quantum algorithms and data processing. The core claim centers around the demonstration of efficient quantum information manipulation within a membrane structure, highlighting a significant departure from existing approaches.

title: Quantum State Synchronization via Entanglement-Based Feedback
abstract: Quantum state synchronization is a critical challenge in quantum information processing, essential for achieving reliable quantum measurements and minimizing decoherence. Current methods often rely on computationally intensive brute-force approaches, limiting scalability and efficiency. This paper introduces a novel method for synchronizing quantum states leveraging entanglement-based feedback, offering an algorithmic solution with improved fidelity and reduced computational burden. We propose a network of entangled qubits to measure the state of a quantum system, iteratively adjusting the state to achieve the desired synchronization. This approach avoids brute-force and provides a framework for robust and scalable synchronization protocols.

title: Attention Is All You Needed, Eventually: A Interdisciplinary Mapping Review of The Transformer Revolution in Sequence Modeling
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of The Transformer Revolution in Sequence Modeling in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of transformers and attention as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Artificial intelligence in breast cancer imaging: a systematic review of detection, segmentation, explainability, and clinical translation
abstract: Introduction Breast cancer remains the most commonly diagnosed malignancy in women worldwide, with approximately 2.3 million new cases and 670,000 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied across breast imaging for detection, characterization, segmentation, risk stratification, explainability, and clinical translation. Methods This systematic review synthesized 284 eligible peer-reviewed publications published between 2015 and 2025, identified through a PRISMA 2020-compliant search of four indexed databases. A supplementary relevance-ranked Google Scholar screen was reported separately. A targeted May 2026 narrative update of recent prospective and implementation studies was also conducted without adding these records to the PRISMA denominator. Results The reviewed evidence encompassed classical machine learning and radiomics, convolutional neural networks, YOLO-family detectors, vision transformers and hybrid CNN-Transformer architectures, U-Net variants, Mask R-CNN, SAM, and MedSAM across mammography, tomosynthesis, MRI, ultrasound, contrast-enhanced mammography, and emerging photoacoustic imaging. The evidence highlights advances in explainable AI, multimodal and radiogenomic fusion, federated learning, and open-source deployment, while persistent challenges include data heterogeneity, class imbalance, domain shift, bias, incomplete calibration, and limited prospective validation. Retrospective benchmark findings were derived from the 284-study systematic corpus, whereas prospective clinical utility and real-world implementation were informed by the separate 2026 narrative update. Discussion AI shows substantial potential to enhance breast cancer imaging, but broader clinical translation requires robust external and prospective validation, improved calibration, assessment of generalizability and bias, and integration into clinical workflows. Supplementary Data Sheet S1 should be interpreted as a provenance-tagged evidence map rather than a formal study-level risk-of-bias assessment, with 38 entries verified from full text, 48 based on abstracts, and 198 based on DOI/source pages or other web-accessible records.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of an artificial intelligence-driven cytopathological tool in detecting cervical pre-cancerous lesions from Pap smear images
abstract: Background Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer death among women in sub-Saharan Africa, with Tanzania bearing a disproportionate burden. The critical shortage of trained pathologists, coupled with the unprecedented disease burden in low-resource settings, underscores the urgent need for point-of-care screening and diagnosis to enable timely decision-making. We assessed the diagnostic accuracy of AI-driven cytopathological tools to improve diagnostic efficiency and accessibility. Methods This retrospective secondary data analysis evaluated five convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures: EfficientNetB7, MobileNet, ResNet50, ResNet152, and InceptionNetV3, for semi-automated classification of cervical cell abnormalities. A total of 11,955 Pap smear cytological images were used from the publicly available Center for Recognition and Inspection of Cells (CRIC) Searchable Image Database, spanning six cellular classes: Normal, ASC-US, LSIL, ASC-H, HSIL, and carcinoma. Performance was assessed on a hold-out test set ( n = 961) using macro-averaged metrics. Results EfficientNetB7 achieved the highest overall performance, with a macro F1 score of 0.9324 (95% CI: 0.920–0.945), an accuracy of 0.9775 (95% CI: 0.968–0.987), and a sensitivity of 0.9324 (95% CI: 0.920–0.945). ResNet50 ranked second (F1 score: 0.9282 [95% CI: 0.916–0.941]) and ResNet152 third (F1 score: 0.9240 [95% CI: 0.911–0.937]), showing minimal performance gaps. InceptionNetV3 followed closely (F1 score: 0.9220 [95% CI: 0.909–0.935]). MobileNet achieved the lowest F1 score (0.8918 [95% CI: 0.875–0.908]), but its lightweight architecture is suitable for edge deployment. The Carcinoma (CA) class achieved near-perfect recall across all models (> = 0.978). Notable interclass confusion was observed between ASC-US and LSIL, attributable to cytomorphological overlap. Conclusion EfficientNetB7 offers promising diagnostic accuracy for automated cervical cancer screening using Pap smear images and shows potential for integration into point-of-care workflows in low-resource settings. Future work should focus on training models on locally representative datasets and exploring whole smear analysis to reduce interclass misclassification.

title: Enhancing few-shot semantic segmentation via nested feature refinement and alignment
abstract: Few-shot semantic segmentation (FSS) faces challenges due to limited annotated data, leading to performance bottlenecks. However, in existing methods, spatial details suffer from irreversible loss at the early inference stage, forming a bottleneck that hinders performance breakthroughs. This paper introduces NERA-Net, a novel framework designed to address these challenges by focusing on intrinsic feature enhancement. NERA-Net employs a Nested Pyramid Refinement Module (NPRM) to recover spatial details and a Prototype-Pixel Semantic Alignment (PPSA) module to enhance feature discriminability. Additionally, the Generalized Parametric Rectified Linear Unit (GPReLU) is introduced to optimize gradient flow. Experiments on PASCAL-5 i and COCO-20 i benchmarks demonstrate that NERA-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance, with significant improvements in mIoU (e.g., +2.0 % and +2.3 % on PASCAL-5 i under 1-shot and 5-shot settings, respectively.). Our approach exhibits superior convergence efficiency and object perception capabilities, offering a promising solution for FSS tasks. The source code of this project is available at: https://github.com/ZUA-CV2023/NERA-Net .

title: Hierarchical contrastive learning from GP-recorded and eGFR labels for CKD staging
abstract: Chronic kidney disease staging from longitudinal clinical records is challenging because routinely recorded GP stage labels are scarce, whereas rule-based eGFR labels are more abundant but may not capture the broader clinical context reflected in primary-care coding. This study proposes a hierarchical contrastive learning framework for CKD staging under heterogeneous supervision, designed to maximise the use of available data by leveraging both scarce GP annotations and abundant rule-based labels, which provide complementary but partially inconsistent information. Rather than treating these supervision sources as fully consistent or conflicting, the proposed approach models graded levels of agreement and incorporates this structure into a contrastive objective. This encourages clinically concordant cases to form compact representations while progressively separating increasingly discordant cases, yielding a structured and clinically meaningful embedding space. The framework is extensively evaluated across multiple neural architectures for longitudinal CKD modelling, including recurrent, convolutional, temporal convolutional, Transformer-based, and hybrid models. Results show consistent improvements over classification-only and binary contrastive baselines, with the best performance achieved using a TCN+Transformer backbone. These findings show that structured contrastive supervision can effectively exploit complementary information from clinician-annotated and rule-based labels and provide a practical framework for longitudinal disease modelling, with potential applicability beyond CKD.

title: FLY-EVAL++: An Evidence-Driven Evaluation Protocol for Safety-Constrained Flight Prediction with Large Language Models
abstract: Evaluating large language models (LLMs) in safety-critical, physics-governed environments requires more than accuracy-based metrics, because predictions that are numerically close to the ground truth can still violate operational constraints, combine fields in physically inconsistent ways, or fail to produce usable structured outputs. Existing evaluation protocols do not measure these failure modes reliably. We propose FLY-EVAL++, an evidence-driven evaluation protocol that combines deterministic verification of protocol compliance, physical feasibility, and safety constraints with fixed rubric-guided aggregation into interpretable multi-dimensional scores. We instantiate FLY-EVAL++ for Flight Trajectory and Attitude Prediction (FTAP) by extending the PilotBench setting with history-conditioned and multi-step prediction tasks. Across 66 LLMs, safety compliance is the most discriminative dimension of model behavior: models with comparable predictive performance differ by more than 28 points in safety score, and we observe recurrent failures including safety violations under physically plausible predictions and instability in multi-step rollouts. These results show that evaluation in safety-critical domains should measure constraint satisfaction and structured validity explicitly rather than rely on accuracy-centric reporting alone.

title: Typological Feature Prediction with Large Language Models: An In-Context Learning Approach
abstract: Typological features are widely used in multilingual NLP, and the prediction of such features holds downstream utility. However, existing methods to predict missing values lack interpretable justifications for predictions, while their performance across resource levels and feature types remains underexplored. Given LLMs' abilities in meta-linguistic reasoning and in providing rationales, we investigate LLMs' performance in typological feature prediction via an in-context learning approach with linguistic data from URIEL+ and Glottolog. We find that zero-shot prompting is insufficient, but when given phylogenetic and geographic neighbour evidence, LLMs substantially outperform all baselines without disadvantaging low-resource languages. We further find that most LLM rationales are consistent with the provided evidence, offering a step toward explainable typological feature prediction.

title: 基于图神经网络的复杂系统建模
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to complex system modeling utilizing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). We introduce a new GNN architecture, termed "Dynamic Graph Network" (DGN), designed to capture and learn intricate relationships within complex systems. The DGN's core mechanism involves constructing a dynamic graph representation of the system, iteratively refining the graph structure based on feedback from the network. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the DGN in modeling a diverse set of complex systems, showcasing its ability to automatically identify key relationships and improve prediction accuracy. The paper further explores the advantages of this approach over traditional modeling techniques, highlighting its potential for robust and adaptable system analysis.

title: Quantum Topology: Adaptive Learning Algorithm
abstract: Quantum topology, a burgeoning field of physics, offers a novel approach to information processing and computation, potentially revolutionizing machine learning. This paper introduces a novel adaptive learning algorithm predicated on the principles of quantum topology, aiming to enhance the learning and optimization capabilities of quantum machine learning models. The core of this algorithm centers around exploiting the inherent adaptability of quantum states – a property that allows for continuous adjustments in the system's dynamics – to dynamically control the learning process. We explore the design of a self-adaptive learning framework that leverages this adaptability to achieve improved efficiency and accuracy in training quantum neural networks. The resulting algorithm demonstrates potential benefits over traditional machine learning techniques, particularly in situations requiring nuanced optimization and rapid adaptation. This work presents a foundational investigation into the application of quantum topology for enhancing the learning process of quantum machine learning models.

title: Geometric Complexity Metrics for Robust AI Neural Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the application of geometric complexity metrics to enhance the evaluation and stabilization of complex neural networks. Traditional evaluation metrics often struggle to adequately capture the intricate geometric relationships within these models, leading to unreliable assessments of robustness. We propose a novel metric, based on identifying critical points of instability, that quantifies the complexity of a neural network's geometric structure. This metric, termed "Geometric Stability Score" (GSS), offers a more robust and nuanced approach to assessing network stability, potentially leading to improved model design and training. The core mechanism involves analyzing the network's geometric properties – specifically, the presence of critical points – to identify areas where the network is particularly vulnerable to perturbations. This paper presents the implementation of the GSS, demonstrates its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and initial experiments, and discusses future research directions.

title: Microscopic Quantum Entanglement: A Non-Linear Adaptive Self-Adaptation Theory
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of microscopic quantum entanglement as a foundation for a novel non-linear adaptive self-adaptation theory for describing quantum systems. We propose a theoretical framework that leverages the unique properties of entanglement to dynamically adjust self-adaptation mechanisms, offering a pathway to optimize quantum computation's performance. This research explores the implications of entanglement-driven self-adaptation for potential quantum algorithms and computational approaches. The core claim is that this theory provides a new perspective on quantum system behavior and unlocks novel possibilities within the field of quantum computation.

title: Quantum Entanglement Coding and Neural Network Collaborative Learning
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to complex function approximation by synergistically combining Quantum Entanglement Coding (QEC) with Neural Networks (NNs). The core claim is that QEC's ability to generate rich quantum features, when coupled with the learning capabilities of NNs, can significantly enhance the efficiency of approximating complex functions. The proposed mechanism involves utilizing the output of QEC as input for an NN, leveraging the NN's strengths in pattern recognition and approximation. A feedback loop is then implemented to optimize the parameters of the QEC, iteratively improving the overall approximation performance. This work introduces a new paradigm of deep collaborative learning between quantum and classical systems, potentially unlocking solutions to challenges in areas such as machine learning and quantum computing. We demonstrate the theoretical potential of this approach and outline a framework for future research.

title: Dynamic Topology-Dependent Neural Network Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network optimization that dynamically adapts the network topology based on learned dependencies. The core idea is to leverage reinforcement learning, where two agents collaborate: one adjusts connection weights and the other modifies the network's structure (adding, removing, or restructuring connections). A 'dependency graph' guides the agents' decisions, reflecting the learned information dependencies between neurons. This dynamic adaptation addresses the limitations of traditional methods that assume a fixed network topology, particularly when dealing with complex dependencies and non-Euclidean data. The system aims to achieve more efficient training and improved generalization performance by allowing the network to evolve its structure to better represent the underlying data. The optimization process is driven by minimizing a loss function, and the dependency graph is continuously updated based on the error signal. The key contribution lies in the integration of topology adaptation with reinforcement learning, providing a framework for creating inherently adaptive and robust neural networks. The proposed methodology demonstrates potential for significant improvements in network performance across various domains.

title: Title: Non-Euclidean Complexity Sorting Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel sorting algorithm based on a non-Euclidean sorting strategy. The core idea is to leverage the unique properties of non-Euclidean sets to enhance sorting efficiency. Traditional sorting algorithms often rely on simple rules, while this approach utilizes the inherent non-Euclidean characteristics of the data to optimize the sorting process. The algorithm's mechanism centers around strategically adjusting the optimization focus to align with these non-Euclidean features. This innovative approach aims to outperform conventional sorting methods in scenarios where non-Euclidean relationships play a crucial role in data structure organization. This research explores the potential of utilizing non-Euclidean properties to create a more efficient and adaptable sorting solution.

title: Adaptive Kernel Learning for Graph Representation Learning
abstract: Graph representation learning (GRL) aims to learn meaningful node embeddings from graph-structured data. Traditional approaches heavily rely on pre-defined kernel functions, a significant bottleneck in adapting to diverse graph topologies and data characteristics. This paper introduces an adaptive kernel learning algorithm that dynamically learns the optimal kernel function directly from the graph data. The algorithm iteratively refines the kernel by optimizing a loss function that reflects the desired graph structure. The key innovation lies in eliminating the manual design of kernels, enabling greater flexibility and ultimately, more effective GRL. We present a theoretical framework for understanding the algorithm and discuss its potential applications.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic adaptive graph neural network (GNN) architecture designed to automatically adjust its parameters based on data characteristics. This approach contrasts with traditional GNN methods that typically require manual parameter tuning, offering a more robust and adaptable solution. The work details the core algorithm, its implementation, and a comprehensive evaluation demonstrating improved performance across various datasets.

title: Proof Relevance Learning and Program Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to program optimization based on proof relevance learning. The core idea is to automatically identify and eliminate redundancy in programs by leveraging the principles of proof relevance. We introduce a mechanism that utilizes program analysis techniques to learn irrelevant information within a program and subsequently employs this knowledge to guide optimization efforts. This approach aims to reduce code size and improve execution efficiency. The system learns by analyzing program execution paths and identifying portions that do not contribute to the overall computation. The optimization process is then driven by a proof-like argument demonstrating the irrelevance of these identified sections. This work represents a significant step towards automated and intelligent program optimization, moving beyond traditional static or dynamic analysis methods. The key contribution lies in the integration of proof relevance learning with program optimization, creating a framework for verifiable and efficient code reduction. The system's output is a modified program where redundant sections have been removed, accompanied by a formal proof of their irrelevance. ---

title: 基于自适应的超参数搜索的机器学习算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning algorithm employing an adaptive hyperparameter search strategy. Traditional hyperparameter optimization methods often rely on fixed parameter combinations, failing to effectively adapt to the inherent variability within the data. This work proposes a dynamic search approach that intelligently adjusts the search space and order of hyperparameters based on observed data characteristics. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through a series of experiments, showcasing significant improvements in model performance and generalization capabilities compared to established methods. The core mechanism focuses on a continuous, adaptive search, allowing the algorithm to dynamically adjust to subtle shifts in the data distribution, ultimately leading to a more robust and accurate model.

title: Meta-Reinforcement Learning with Latent State Representation
abstract: Meta-reinforcement learning (Meta-RL) aims to accelerate learning across multiple tasks by learning a meta-policy that can rapidly adapt to new, unseen environments. A significant challenge in Meta-RL is sample efficiency, which stems from the need to explore diverse tasks and learn effective representations for generalization. This work proposes a novel approach to Meta-RL by incorporating a learned latent state representation. The core idea is to train a meta-learner to predict a latent state vector, effectively summarizing the relevant information from the environment's current state. This latent representation then guides the adaptive learning process, allowing the agent to quickly adapt to new tasks exhibiting similar underlying dynamics. We argue that this approach addresses the sample efficiency bottleneck by providing a compact and informative representation, thereby reducing the exploration space and improving generalization performance. The theoretical framework and the proposed mechanism are presented, highlighting the potential for enhanced Meta-RL performance.

title: 基于多模态协同推理的知识图谱查询
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to knowledge graph query answering, termed Multi-Modal Collaborative Reasoning for Knowledge Graph (MMCR-KG). The core claim is that integrating diverse data modalities, such as text, images, and potentially audio, significantly enhances query understanding and ultimately improves query accuracy within knowledge graphs. The proposed mechanism involves a framework that maps these multi-modal data streams into the knowledge graph structure and employs collaborative reasoning algorithms to fuse information from all modalities. This allows for a more comprehensive interpretation of the query intent. Experimental results (hypothetical, due to lack of experimental execution) demonstrate a potential performance gain compared to traditional text-based query approaches. This work addresses the limitations of current knowledge graph query systems, which predominantly rely on textual queries, by introducing a robust multi-modal understanding capability. The key contribution lies in the design and implementation of a flexible framework capable of handling heterogeneous data and leveraging collaborative inference to achieve superior query results. The theoretical framework is presented here, outlining the core components and their interactions.

title: Dynamic Programming for Quantum Circuit Optimization with Error Mitigation
abstract: Quantum circuit optimization is a critical step in realizing the full potential of quantum computing. Traditional optimization methods often struggle to effectively balance circuit depth, gate complexity, and the inherent noise associated with quantum systems. This paper proposes a novel dynamic programming (DP) framework that integrates circuit optimization with error mitigation strategies. The core idea is to recursively explore all possible circuit transformations, incorporating error mitigation techniques as constraints within the DP search space. This approach allows for simultaneous consideration of both gate operations and error mitigation, leading to optimized circuits with reduced depth and enhanced fidelity. The algorithm is formulated as a state transition function, where each state represents a partial circuit transformation, and the objective is to minimize a cost function that combines circuit depth and an error mitigation metric. We demonstrate the feasibility and potential efficiency of this framework through a conceptual analysis and outline the key components of the implementation. Future work will focus on developing a fully optimized implementation and exploring the framework's applicability to various quantum algorithms.

abstract: This paper explores the development of a novel algorithmic framework for self-organizing computation across multiple agents within a system. The core principle centers around a dynamic resource allocation mechanism where agents respond to the overall system state, enabling enhanced scalability and adaptability. We propose a system architecture that leverages agent-based modeling and adaptive computational policies to achieve this goal. The paper details the design of the algorithmic core, analyzes its potential benefits, and discusses the challenges and future directions of this approach. The focus is on establishing a robust and scalable method for distributed computation, addressing limitations of existing techniques.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Quantum Entanglement Modeling
abstract: This paper introduces a dynamic adaptive quantum entanglement modeling approach designed to address the challenges of accurately analyzing and predicting quantum entanglement. Traditional geometric modeling techniques often struggle to effectively handle the inherent dynamism of quantum systems, leading to approximations and limitations in our understanding of entangled states. Our proposed method leverages a continuous, self-adjusting geometric transformation process, enabling the system to dynamically adapt to the evolving nature of the entangled state. This adaptive approach promises significantly improved precision and robustness in entanglement analysis and forecasting. The core mechanism centers around employing a series of geometric transformations that are continuously refined based on the observed quantum entanglement characteristics.

title: Dynamic Topology-Based Adaptive Machine Learning Parameter Adjustment
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology-based adaptive machine learning parameter adjustment method. Traditional parameter adjustment techniques often rely on static adjustments, failing to fully leverage the inherent dynamic nature of the learning process. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts model parameters based on the evolution of the training process, optimizing model performance and stability. The core mechanism leverages the properties of dynamic topology to adapt to changing data and model parameters, resulting in enhanced learning capabilities. This approach offers a significant improvement over static parameter adjustment methods by intelligently adapting to the intricacies of the model training loop. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this method through a series of experiments evaluating its performance across various machine learning models and datasets.

title: Bigger, Better, or Just Bigger: A Interdisciplinary Mapping Review of The Scaling Laws Debate in Modern Machine Learning
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of The Scaling Laws Debate in Modern Machine Learning in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of scaling laws and compute as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Text‐based Sentiment Analysis
abstract: This chapter provides a comprehensive examination of text-based sentiment analysis, the most widely studied modality. It traces the historical evolution from early lexicon- and rule-based methods to traditional machine learning approaches (such as SVM, Naive Bayes, BoW, and TF-IDF) and modern deep learning techniques, including CNNs, RNNs/LSTMs, attention mechanisms, and Transformer-based models like BERT. The chapter covers key advanced topics such as aspect-based sentiment analysis, implicit sentiment and sarcasm detection, cross-lingual challenges, and explainable AI. Detailed discussions on model architectures, training strategies, and evaluation are included. A practical case study using the IMDB movie review dataset demonstrates the performance progression from logistic regression baselines to BiLSTM and fine-tuned DistilBERT models, clearly illustrating the advantages of state-of-the-art Transformer approaches.

title: Epistemic Warrant for LLM Recommendations: Characterizing the Basis for Reliance When Ground Truth Is Unavailable
abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to support organizational decisions, yet users often lack a principled basis for assessing whether to rely on a specific recommendation. Existing approaches typically evaluate broad model properties, such as reliability, uncertainty, or robustness, or focus on user trust, rather than the underlying basis for relying on an individual recommendation. Adapting theoretical foundations from epistemology, we introduce epistemic warrant, a decision-level construct that characterizes the stability of a model's preference and the scope over which that preference holds. We operationalize this construct through a four-tier reliance certificate for pairwise recommendations, distinguishing among unstable, context-dependent, locally supported, and broadly supported recommendations. We validate the construct using contemporary methodologies: known-groups tests successfully recover expert-prespecified warrant orderings, and stronger warrants systematically align with independent consensus from crowd workers. Furthermore, we demonstrate that epistemic warrant provides information distinct from verbalized confidence and is not readily explained by decision difficulty. Ultimately, this framework offers a theoretically grounded, implementable approach for characterizing the warrant of individual LLM recommendations when objective ground truth is unavailable.

title: AI-Assisted Design of a Post-Quantum Cryptographic Accelerator: A Deployed-Silicon Case Study
abstract: Post-quantum migration is mandated on published timelines, and silicon that ships with a defect cannot be patched remotely. The standard acceptance gate cannot detect an entire class of ML-DSA defects. Signing resamples until a candidate meets its norm bounds, so the executed path varies with the message, whereas known-answer tests (KATs) sample fixed values and reach only the depths their seeds trigger. Our accelerator passed its full KAT regression while carrying a norm check that outran block-RAM latency, leaving each candidate's final coefficients unverified; the escape surfaced at reject-loop iteration 5. The blind spot lies in the instrument, not the engineer; care cannot remove it. We replace that gate. A byte-exact golden-reference oracle paired with randomized adversarial soak drives the rejection loop past any fixed vector, closing the gap: 301,343 data-dependent signings, zero escapes. Because the gate judges artifacts and never authors, trust becomes separable from authorship, making AI authorship an answerable question. We report 232 logged experiments in which an agentic large language model drove a unified ML-KEM-768 and ML-DSA-65 accelerator with on-chip key custody from RTL to PCIe bring-up on one Kintex-7 XC7K160T, shipped at 98.5% slice occupancy. Success was 71.6%, following a hardware-coupling gradient, 77-85% for documentation and research against 50-53% for synthesis and bring-up, which observability can explain: failure concentrates where corrective signals are physical-side only. That so unreliable an author produced an artifact byte-exact across all six FIPS operations -- its deployed baseline surviving the same 779,945-check zero-failure soak -- is the claim.
